source.title: Weil representation and Arithmetic Fundamental Lemma
source.version: Published 116-page journal PDF, read in full; public YMSC mirror verified against publisher metadata. Author preprint collated selectively; Mihatsch–Zhang, DOI10.4171/JEMS/1375, §7.2 footnote5 supplies a published Gaussian correction.
readSections: §§2–5 local orbits, FL/AFL, Cayley reduction and local constancy
§§6–10 unitary models, derived CM cycles, modularity and local intersections
§§11–12 Weil representation, regularized RTF and partial Gaussians
Appendix A, Appendix B and all 47 references

Review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (Claude Code, cc-39fac3, 23 September 2026): the published PDF (same SHA-256 6f8ac537…) read in full again with four checkers; every item checked against it; the author's preprint and Mihatsch–Zhang (JEMS) consulted for the corrections.

published.version: Published journal PDF mirrored by YMSC; title, page range, DOI and April2021 metadata match publisher.

author.read: Selective collation of Cayley, KR morphisms, §12 Gaussian/chart formulas and §14 comparison; not a whole-preprint reading.
readSections: Cayley factor and KR morphism collation
§14 holomorphic comparison and E definition; §15 nearby-space sentence

provenance.history: arXiv1909.02697 v1 6Sep2019,v2 9Jun2020,v3 20Dec2020(final). Abstract omits odd-prime/strongly-regular qualifications present in published body. No whole-arXiv reading claim. The author PDF is an earlier 78-page version with shifted lemma numbering, not asserted identical to the journal.

correctionSource.finding: Explicit printed correction to Zhang2021 §12 Gaussian functions, and explicit Whittaker normalization; not a whole-paper reading or substitute for original main theorem.

summary: Zhang proves the arithmetic fundamental lemma for strongly regular semisimple elements over Q_p for p ≥ n (Theorem 15.1), together with the Jacquet–Rallis fundamental lemma for q ≥ n (Theorem 13.9), by induction on n through a global comparison. Modularity of arithmetic generating series of derived CM cycles on unitary Shimura varieties is matched with a regularized relative trace formula for partial Gaussian test functions, using that the Weil representation commutes with smooth transfer (Appendix A). Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and twenty-eight findings are recorded. The partial-Gaussian descent of §12.4 (E16, E17), the Gaussian normalization (E12, E15, corrected by Mihatsch–Zhang) and the Proposition 3.9 bound in the final induction (E28) are proof issues with repairs; the main theorems stand. Not formalised. After the review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21) there are 176 items (7 library, 13 planned, 156 missing) and 60 source issues. The most consequential new finding is that the proof of Proposition 4.12(i) (and 2.7(i)) does not cover q = n, so the printed proof of the AFL (Theorem 15.1(a)) at p = n has a gap; the FL at q = n is covered by Beuzart-Plessis, and all cases with q ≥ n + 1 are unaffected.

items.name: Hermitian-to-quadratic convention
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero quadratic extension F/F0, an F/F0-Hermitian form is linear in its first argument. Its F0-quadratic form is q(u)=h(u,u); its associated bilinear form is TrF/F0 h and has diagonal 2q. Norm fibres are Vξ={u:q(u)=ξ}.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.2 (hermitian local theory) is a plausible owner for this convention. The paper's §1.2 misprints the codomain of q (E1, confirmed); the item already uses the corrected F0-valued form.
api: Construct scalar restriction, trace bilinear form and norm fibres; distinguish the pairings by type.
Export orthogonal decomposition and isometry transport.
unitTests: The standard Hermitian line has real bilinear diagonal 2|z|².

items.name: Schwartz spaces and Fourier transform
items.statement: For a smooth algebraic variety X over a local field F: if F is non-archimedean, S(X(F)) is the space of locally constant compactly supported functions; if F is archimedean, S(X(F)) is the space of smooth φ with Dφ bounded for every algebraic differential operator D on X; S(X(A)) is the restricted tensor product. ψ = ψ_Q∘tr_{F0/Q}, ψ_ξ(x) = ψ(ξx). For a quadratic space (V, q) with ⟨x,y⟩ = q(x+y)−q(x)−q(y), the Fourier transform is φ̂(x) = ∫_{V(F_v)} φ(y) ψ_v(⟨x,y⟩) dy with dy the self-dual Haar measure.
items.locator: §1.2 (Notation on automorphic forms), p. 870; §11.1 (11.1) and the Fourier transform, pp. 932–933
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Minor: 'algebraically rapidly decreasing' paraphrases the archimedean definition. The paper's condition (p. 870) is: smooth φ on X(F) such that Dφ is bounded for every algebraic differential operator D on X. The locator lacks pages. Review note: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.0 plans exactly this (Schwartz–Bruhat spaces, Fourier transforms, self-dual measures); status planned is right.
api: Construct partial Fourier transforms and seminorm estimates; compare the positive Fourier sign with Mathlib's convention.
unitTests: Double transform is reflection; an arbitrary Haar measure is not self-dual.

items.name: SL2 automorphic and coefficient-valued forms
items.statement: Let F0 be totally real and H = SL2. For h ∈ SL2(R), write h = n(b) m(a^{1/2}) κ_θ with a > 0, b ∈ R and κ_θ ∈ SO(2). The weight-k Whittaker function is W^{(k)}_ξ(h) = a^{k/2} e^{2πiξ(b+ia)} e^{ikθ} ((1.5)–(1.8)). A_hol(Γ,k) (Γ(N) ⊂ Γ ⊂ SL2(Z)) and A_hol(H(A0),K,k) (moderate growth, right K-invariant, of parallel weight k, killed by ½(i 1; 1 −i) at every real place) are finite-dimensional, with Q-structures given by q-expansion at i∞. A_hol(·)_L ⊗_L W is the space of formal q^{1/N}-series with W-coefficients that are finite L-combinations of q-expansions ((1.9)–(1.10)). For a weight-k φ, set φ♭_{h_f}(τ) = |a∞|^{−k/2} φ(h∞, h_f) (1.11); if φ ∈ A_hol(H(A0),K,k), then φ♭_{h_f} ∈ A_hol(h_f K h_f^{−1} ∩ H(F0), k). For a left N(F0)-invariant continuous φ, W_{φ,ξ}(h) = ∫_{F0\A0} φ(n(b)h) ψ(−ξb) db, with db of total mass 1 (1.12). For smooth φ, φ(h) = Σ_{ξ∈F0} W_{φ,ξ}(h), absolutely (1.13); for merely continuous φ, only uniqueness of Fourier coefficients holds. For F0 = Q only: A_exp(H(A),K,k) consists of the smooth, left H(Q)-invariant, right K-invariant, weight-k functions with |φ(h∞h_f)| ≤ e^{Ca} as a → ∞ whose image under the lowering operator ½(i 1; 1 −i) lies in A_hol(H(A),K,k−2).
items.locator: §1.2 (Notation on automorphic forms), (1.5)–(1.13) and the definition of A_exp, pp. 870–872
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Two points. (1) A_exp is defined only for F0 = Q (p. 872), with the growth bound |φ(h∞h_f)| ≤ e^{Ca} as a → ∞; the item's 'Over totally real F0' covers A_hol but not A_exp. (2) (1.13) holds absolutely only for smooth φ (E2, confirmed), and requires db on F0\A0 of total mass 1, which the paper leaves implicit. The API line already asks for smoothness. The locator lacks pages.
api: Construct adelic/classical conversion φ↦φ♭, Fourier coefficient and coefficient extension.
Require smoothness for absolute Fourier reconstruction, not mere continuity.
unitTests: Wξ(1)=exp(−2πξ).
Nonzero constants cannot have nonzero weight.

items.name: Group, Lie and semi-Lie relative spaces
items.statement: Let n ≥ 2, e = (0,…,0,1)^T ∈ F^n, and embed GL_{n−1} ↪ GL_n by γ0 ↦ diag(γ0, 1) (the elements fixing e and e*). Set S_n = {γ ∈ Res_{F/F0}GL_n : γγ̄ = 1} and s_n = {y ∈ Res_{F/F0}M_n : y + ȳ = 0}. H′ = GL_{n−1} acts on both by h·γ = h^{−1}γh, and on S_{n−1} × V′_{n−1}, V′_{n−1} = F0^{n−1} × (F0^{n−1})*, by h·(γ,(u1,u2)) = (h^{−1}γh, (h^{−1}u1, u2h)), and likewise on s_{n−1} × V′_{n−1}. Unitary side: V♯ is an n-dimensional F/F0-hermitian space with a non-isotropic special vector u0, V = u0^⊥, G = U(V♯) and H = U(V) acting by conjugation on G, on u(V♯), and diagonally on U(V) × V and u(V) × V. The special vector is normalised to norm 1 from §2.2 on.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Minor: 'embed GL(n−1) diagonally in GLn' is ambiguous. The paper embeds by γ0 ↦ diag(γ0, 1), that is, as the stabiliser of e and e* (2.1). S_n and s_n are Res_{F/F0}-schemes over F0. The locator lacks pages.
api: Construct actions, homogeneous/group adapters and block embeddings; expose ambient and acting ranks separately.
unitTests: GL1 acts on S2.
The row transforms contragrediently.

items.name: Relative orbit matching
items.statement: There are bijections ⊔_V [U(V♯)(F0)]_rs ≅ [S_n(F0)]_rs (2.6) and ⊔_V [(U(V)×V)(F0)]_rs ≅ [(S_{n−1}×V′_{n−1})(F0)]_rs (2.7), with analogous identifications on the Lie algebras (2.8)–(2.9); V runs over the isometry classes of (n−1)-dimensional F/F0-hermitian spaces and V♯ = V ⊕ F u0 with ⟨u0,u0⟩ = 1. g and γ (resp. (g,u) and (γ,(u1,u2))) match when their images in Res_{F/F0}M_n (via (g,u) ↦ (g u; u* 0) and (γ,(u1,u2)) ↦ (γ u1; u2 0)) are conjugate under Res_{F/F0}GL_{n−1}. Equivalently, det(T + g) = det(T + γ) and ⟨g^i u, u⟩ = u2 γ^i u1 for 0 ≤ i ≤ n−2. These invariants identify both categorical quotients with B_{n−1} ⊂ Res_{F/F0}(F[T]_{deg=n−1} × F^{n−1}).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Minor omissions. The index range of the moment invariants is 0 ≤ i ≤ n−2. The Lie-algebra analogues (2.8)–(2.9), used in §12.2 and implicitly in the Lie-algebra steps of Lemmas 4.10–4.11 and 5.4, are left out.
items.proofOutline: Reconstruct the nonsingular Hermitian Gram matrix in a cyclic-vector basis from the moments. Prove the homogeneous, group and Lie adapters independently; this is not stable endoscopic matching.

items.name: Invariant quotient and reciprocal polynomial
items.statement: An parametrizes monic conjugate-self-reciprocal degree-n polynomials with nonzero constant term; B records characteristic coefficients and moments. Preserve det(T+g) versus det(T−g) conventions. Irreducible α implies nonzero unitary vectors are cyclic; CM compactness is an additional condition.
items.locator: §2.2 (2.10)–(2.11), pp. 875–876 (the fixed-field and cyclicity remarks come from §7.4 and §12.6)
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Checked (2.11) on the page image: T^{deg α} α(T^{−1}) = α(0) ᾱ(T), whence α(0)ᾱ(0) = 1. The item's paraphrase is faithful.
api: Construct quotient map, discriminant open, sign adapter and refined invariants.
unitTests: T²−3T+1 over Q(i) is reciprocal but its specified fixed field is imaginary.

items.name: Orbital integrals and transfer factors
items.statement: Let F/F0 be a quadratic extension of local fields of characteristic 0, η = η_{F/F0}, and η̃ a fixed extension of η to F^× (η̃(x) = (−1)^{v(x)} when F/F0 is unramified). For γ ∈ S_n(F0)_rs, Orb(γ,f′,s) = ∫_{GL_{n−1}(F0)} f′(h^{−1}γh) |det h|^s η(det h) dh (2.12). For (γ,u′) ∈ (S_{n−1}×V′_{n−1})(F0)_rs, Orb((γ,u′),Φ′,s) = ∫_{GL_{n−1}(F0)} Φ′(h^{−1}γh, h^{−1}u1, u2h) |det h|^s η(det h) dh (2.14). Orb(γ,f′) = ω(γ) Orb(γ,f′,0) and ∂Orb(γ,f′) = ω(γ) (d/ds)|_{s=0} Orb(γ,f′,s) (2.13), and likewise with ω(γ,u′), where ω(γ) = η̃(det(γ)^{−⌊n/2⌋} det(γ^i e)_{0≤i≤n−1}) (2.16) and ω(γ,u′) = η̃(det(γ)^{−⌊(n−1)/2⌋} det(γ^i u1)_{0≤i≤n−2}) (2.17); ω does not depend on s. Unitary side: Orb(g,f) = ∫_{U(V)(F0)} f(h^{−1}gh) dh and Orb((g,u),Φ) = ∫_{U(V)(F0)} Φ(h·(g,u)) dh (2.15), with no character and no transfer factor. In the unramified setting of §2.4, vol(GL_{n−1}(O_{F0})) = vol(K0) = 1.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The integrand direction is ambiguous. 'Φ(h⁻¹·x)' with the paper's action h·(γ,(u1,u2)) = (h^{−1}γh, h^{−1}u1, u2h) is the substitution h ↦ h^{−1}, which changes |det h|^s to |det h|^{−s} and so flips the sign of ∂Orb. The paper integrates f′(h^{−1}γh) and Φ′(h·(γ,u′)) against |det h|^s η(det h) dh ((2.12), (2.14)). The locator lacks pages.
api: Separate raw integral, transferred value and transferred derivative.
For rank r semi-Lie use ω=η̃(det(γ)^−floor(r/2)det(u1,γu1,…,γ^(r−1)u1)); prove conjugation and measure-change laws.
unitTests: Scaling u1 by a contributes η(a)^r.
Do not differentiate ω in s.

items.name: Smooth and partial transfer
items.statement: Linear and unitary test functions match when transferred orbital integrals agree on matching regular semisimple orbits; use two local Hermitian classes nonarchimedean and all signatures over R. Partial transfer fixes α and one Hermitian class and requires vanishing on other classes in that fibre.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Checked against Definition 13.1: partial transfer asks for equality only on matching orbits in the α-fibre for the fixed V_v, and for vanishing of Orb((γ,u′),Φ′_v) on the other orbits of that fibre. Faithful. Definition 2.2 and the line before (2.17) print V_{n−1} for V′_{n−1} (new misprint below).
api: Construct the matching relation on test-function quotient spaces and split-place elementary transfer.
Existence is a theorem, not data assumed in the definition.
unitTests: Agreement on the chosen class does not discharge vanishing on other classes.

items.name: Group Jacquet–Rallis FL
items.statement: Let F0 be a finite extension of Q_p with p odd, F/F0 unramified quadratic, q the residue cardinality of F0, with q ≥ n. Let V♯_0 (split) and V♯_1 (non-split) be the n-dimensional hermitian spaces with special vectors of unit norm, Λ♯_0 = Λ0 ⊕ O_F u0 self-dual, K♯_0 = Stab(Λ♯_0) ⊂ U(V♯_0)(F0), and vol(GL_{n−1}(O_{F0})) = vol(K0) = 1. Then 1_{S_n(O_{F0})} transfers to (1_{K♯_0}, 0).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The hypothesis on F0 is incomplete. The paper's setting (§2.4) is an unramified quadratic extension of a p-adic field (characteristic 0) with p odd; 'odd residue characteristic' alone also admits local fields of characteristic p. The locator lacks pages. Review note: For q = n, Theorem 13.9(a) is obtained from Proposition 2.7(i) at the boundary case, whose printed proof has a gap (new issue on Proposition 4.12(i)/2.7(i); explicit example with q = n = 3). The statement itself is covered for all odd p by Beuzart-Plessis [2], cited in §1.
items.proofOutline: Use the semi-Lie induction and Proposition2.7(i). Correct the printed target K0 to K0#; q is the residue cardinality, not p.

items.name: Semi-Lie Jacquet–Rallis FL
items.statement: Under the same unramified odd hypotheses and q≥n, the unit function on (Sn−1×V′n−1)(OF0) transfers to (1K0×Λ0,0), for the self-dual lattice Λ0 in split dimension n−1.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Statement faithful. As for item 9, F0 is a p-adic field (characteristic 0). Part (b) at q ≥ n does not pass through the boundary case of Proposition 2.7(i).
items.proofOutline: Globalize strongly regular data, compare holomorphic generating functions, isolate an invariant at a split place, then use density and local constancy on the full relative regular locus.

items.name: Maximal-order FL
items.statement: For a regular semi-Lie pair in the split space, if g is full-group regular semisimple and OF[g] is maximal in the degree-r étale algebra F[g], the unit-function FL holds.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: E4 confirmed: the printed (G0 × V0) should be (H0 × V0). The item already uses the correct space.
items.proofOutline: Decompose the étale algebra and count stable self-dual lattices with the prescribed volumes. Correct the printed G0×V0 to the properly ranked semi-Lie space.

items.name: FL rank equivalence
items.statement: Let F/F0 be an unramified quadratic extension of p-adic fields, p odd, q the residue cardinality of F0, with special vectors of unit norm. If q ≥ n, Conjecture 2.3(a) for S_n implies Conjecture 2.3(b) for S_{n−1}×V′_{n−1}. If q ≥ n+1, the converse holds. (Proposition 2.7(i) asserts the equivalence for q ≥ n; its proof does not cover (b) ⇒ (a) at q = n.)
items.locator: §2.4, Proposition 2.7(i), p. 879 (proof by reference to Proposition 4.12, pp. 895–896)
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The printed equivalence (q ≥ n) is not fully proved. For (b) for S_{n−1}×V′_{n−1} ⇒ (a) for S_n at q = n, the proof (by reference to Proposition 4.12) needs ξ ∈ F^1 with both det(1−ξg′) and 1−ξd units, and such ξ need not exist (new gap, explicit example with q = n = 3). The item should record which direction holds under which bound. Review note: The FL analogue of Lemma 4.11 on the unitary side (Orb(g′,1_{K♯_0}) = Orb(r(g′),1_{K0×Λ0}) under (4.21)) is needed here but not stated in the paper: proposed as a new item in coverage.
items.proofOutline: Use central scalars, relative Cayley charts, integral orbit equality and the separate transfer-factor comparison.

items.name: FL norm-unit reduction
items.statement: Under Proposition2.7's hypotheses, group FL for Sn−1 implies dimension-(n−1) semi-Lie FL for vectors of unit norm.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Split off the unit vector integrally, apply lower-rank group FL and compare measures. This does not cover arbitrary norms.

items.name: Unitary Rapoport–Zink moduli
items.statement: For unramified F/F0 with odd residue characteristic, Nn classifies strict formal OF0-modules of relative height 2n and dimension n, OF-action of signature (n−1,1), relative principal polarization with conjugate Rosati, and height-zero polarized quasi-isogeny to a fixed supersingular framing object.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Faithful. The paper phrases it through p-divisible groups of absolute height 2nd and dimension n whose O_{F0}-action on Lie is via the structure map (hence formal O_{F0}-modules of relative height 2n). The framing ρ is a height-0 O_F-linear quasi-isogeny over S̄ = S ×_{Spf O_F̆} Spec k̄ with ρ*((λ_X)_S̄) = λ_S̄, and the Kottwitz condition is char(ι(a) | Lie X) = (T−a)^{n−1}(T−ā).
api: Construct base change, framing action and the relative/absolute height adapter; retain the relative polarization.
unitTests: Absolute height is 2n[F0:Qp].
N1 is Spf O_Fbreve.

items.name: RZ representability and dimension
items.statement: Nn in the preceding unramified odd setting is formally locally of finite type and formally smooth of relative dimension n−1 over Spf O_Fbreve.
items.locator: §3.1, p. 880 (stated without proof; construction cf. [38, §4]). The paper does not cite [31] there.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: The paper states 'N_n is smooth over Spf O_F̆ of relative dimension n−1' without proof. N_{n−1,n} is then formally smooth of formal dimension 2(n−1). The external input is the RZ representability theorem.
items.proofOutline: Import the precise RZ/RSZ deformation theorem and reconcile relative versus absolute models using the Eisenstein condition. External proof closure remains open.

items.name: Framings, special Hom and diagonal
items.statement: Let 𝔼 be the formal O_F-module of signature (1,0) over k̄ (unique up to isomorphism), 𝓔 its canonical lift over O_F̆, and 𝔼̄, 𝓔̄ the conjugate objects of signature (0,1). Take X_1 = 𝔼̄ and X_n = X_{n−1} × 𝔼 as framing objects. For n ≥ 2, δ: N_{n−1} → N_n, (X,ι,λ,ρ) ↦ (X×𝓔, ι×ι_𝓔, λ×λ_𝓔, ρ×ρ_𝓔), is a closed embedding. Δ ⊂ N_{n−1,n} = N_{n−1} ×_{Spf O_F̆} N_n is the image of the graph (id, δ); it is closed of half the formal dimension. V_n := Hom°_{O_F}(𝔼, X_n), with the hermitian form induced by the polarisations, is a non-split n-dimensional hermitian space containing no self-dual lattice. Aut°(X_n, ι, λ) ≅ U(V_n)(F0) (3.6), acting on N_n by g·(X,ι,λ,ρ) = (X,ι,λ,g∘ρ). The inclusion of 𝔼 as the last factor is a special vector u0 of norm 1, V_n = V_{n−1} ⊕ F u0, and δ and Δ are equivariant for U(V_{n−1}) ↪ U(V_n) and U(V_{n−1}) ↪ U(V_{n−1}) × U(V_n).
items.locator: §3.1 (3.2)–(3.6) and the definition of V_n, pp. 880–881
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Imprecise, and 'its conjugate action' is not what the paper does. The paper's framing objects are X_1 = 𝔼̄ (signature (0,1)) and X_n = X_{n−1} × 𝔼, and δ multiplies by the canonical lift 𝓔 of the signature-(1,0) object 𝔼. The identification (3.6) and the U(V_n)(F0)-action on N_n, both used throughout, are omitted. Review note: Checked (3.2)–(3.3) on the page image (p. 880): X_1 = 𝔼̄ is barred, 𝔼 and 𝓔 in (3.2)–(3.3) are not.
api: Make conjugate action explicit rather than dropping overbars; construct adjoint, unit vector, orthogonal complement and δ.
unitTests: The special unit vector has norm one and orthogonal complement Vn−1.

items.name: Local KR divisor
items.statement: For nonzero u∈Vn, Z(u)⊂Nn is the locus where the special quasi-homomorphism lifts to an actual homomorphism. It is empty or a relative Cartier divisor, with gZ(u)=Z(gu) and Z(u0)≅Nn−1 for the unit vector.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct liftability under nilpotent base change, Cartier ideal and equivariance.
unitTests: Do not apply the Cartier theorem to u=0.
Unit norm recovers δ.

items.name: Derived group intersection
items.statement: For relative regular semisimple g∈U(Vn), Int(g)=χ(OΔ⊗L O(1×g)Δ) on Nn−1×Nn, using proper scheme intersection support and O_Fbreve-length.
items.locator: §3.1 (3.8), p. 881 (the homogeneous variant (3.7) for g ∈ G_{V_1}(F0)_rs is on the same page)
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct graph translate, derived support and finite-length Euler characteristic; prove conjugation invariance.
unitTests: Retain higher Tor at nontransverse intersections.

items.name: Derived fixed locus and semi-Lie intersection
items.statement: Ng=Γg∩ΔN is the naive fixed locus; LNg is the K-class OΓg⊗L OΔN transported to N. For regular semisimple (g,u), define Int(g,u)=χ(LNg⊗L OZ(u)); its support is a proper scheme.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Separate naive support from derived class; expose the projection formula on N×N.
unitTests: Simultaneous conjugation preserves Int; arbitrary nonregular pairs need not have proper support.

items.name: Strong regular semisimplicity
items.statement: A semi-Lie regular semisimple pair is strongly regular if its group coordinate is semisimple under full-group conjugation. For relative group orbits require relative regularity and full GLn/U(Vn) semisimplicity. Do not identify these with mere relative regularity.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct the dense loci, cyclic-vector criteria and matching compatibility.
unitTests: Keep relative and full acting groups distinct.

items.name: Strongly regular group AFL
items.statement: For F0=Qp, unramified quadratic F/F0, p odd and p≥n, matching γ∈Sn(F0)srs and g∈U(Vn)(F0)srs satisfy ∂Orb(γ,1Sn(OF0))=−Int(g)log p in the §2 normalization.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Statement faithful. At p = n, part (a) comes from Proposition 4.12(i) at q = n, and the printed argument for (b)_{n−1} ⇒ (a)_n has a gap there (new issue). Parts (a) for p ≥ n+1, and (b), are unaffected.
items.proofOutline: Combine Proposition4.12 with the semi-Lie induction. Conjecture3.2 on all regular semisimple elements is not the proved endpoint.

items.name: Strongly regular semi-Lie AFL
items.statement: Under Theorem15.1's literal indexed hypotheses p odd, F0=Qp and p≥n, matching strongly regular pairs in Sn−1×V′n−1 and U(Vn−1)×Vn−1 satisfy ∂Orb((γ,u′),1integral)=−Int(g,u)log p.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Globalize while preserving the local étale order, apply Corollary14.8 and joint local constancy. Do not silently strengthen the bound by reindexing the proof.

items.name: Maximal-order AFL input
items.statement: In the unramified odd local setting, for p>n and (g,u)∈(U(Vn−1)×Vn−1)srs with OF[g] maximal in F[g], semi-Lie AFL holds.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. (cc-442dc5) Finding E28: in the proof of Theorem 15.1 this is applied in Hermitian dimension n at places with p_v ≥ n only; the places with p_v ≤ n + 1 can be moved to case (ii) of Theorem 14.6. Review note: Statement faithful. The note's E28 sentence is garbled ('places with p_v ≥ n only; the places with p_v ≤ n + 1 can be moved'). What E28 means: in Hermitian dimension n, Proposition 3.9 needs p_v > n+1, while places outside S only satisfy p_v ≥ n, so the places with p_v ∈ {n, n+1} are uncovered and should go to case (ii) of Theorem 14.6. E28 was not in this reviewer's assignment.
items.proofOutline: Import Mihatsch[31] Corollary9.9 and the separate rank-one case. The strict bound and its use in the final induction require external verification; do not weaken p>n by fiat.

items.name: Cayley and relative Schur maps
items.statement: On the invertibility opens, c(x)=−(1−x)(1+x)⁻¹ and c⁻¹(g)=(1+g)(1−g)⁻¹. For g′=[h u;w* d], set g=h+(1−d)⁻¹uw* and r(g′)=(g,u/((1−d)√ε)), with F=F0(√ε), ε∈OF0×; r♭ instead uses the Cayley vector ũ/√ε.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): Naming: the paper's variant is r♮ (natural sign), not r♭ (checked on p. 886). r uses the block vector u, scaled by 1/((1−d)√ε), while r♮ uses the Cayley vector ũ = 2(1−d)^{−1}(1−g)^{−1}u divided by √ε.
api: Make denominator domains explicit; construct central-scalar variants rξ and inverse chart.
unitTests: Both Cayley compositions are identity on their domains.

items.name: Block Cayley identities
items.statement: In Lemma4.1's domain, ũ=2(1−d)⁻¹(1−g)⁻¹u, det(1−g′)=(1−d)det(1−g), and gw=((1−conjugate(d))/(1−d))u, with g the Schur complement above.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Verified numerically for a random g′ ∈ U(4) (standard form over C/R): g = h + (1−d)^{−1}uw* = c(x), ũ = 2(1−d)^{−1}(1−g)^{−1}u, det(1−g′) = (1−d)det(1−g), and gw = ((1−d̄)/(1−d))u all hold. The lower-left block of x′ is −ũ*.
items.proofOutline: Expand (1+g′)=(1−g′)x′, use unitary block equations and the Schur determinant formula; preserve the conjugation bar.

items.name: Relative Cayley open isomorphism
items.statement: Adding the lower-right Lie coordinate e gives an equivariant isomorphism U(Vn)°→(U(Vn−1)×Vn−1×u1)°; the same holds for r♭.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): Minor: the variant is r♮, not r♭. The open sets should be explicit: U(V_n)° = {1−d ≠ 0, det(1−g′) ≠ 0}, and (U(V_{n−1})×V_{n−1}×u(1))° = {det(1−g) ≠ 0, det(1+x′) ≠ 0} with x′ = (x ũ; −ũ* e), x = c^{−1}(g), where ũ = 2√ε(1−g)^{−1}u for r and ũ = √ε u for r♮. Review note: The missing factor 2 in the proof is E5 (confirmed; it is on p. 886, not p. 887).
items.proofOutline: Recover the full Lie block matrix then apply inverse Cayley and verify both determinant predicates. Correct the proof's missing factor 2.

items.name: Cayley regularity and generic strong regularity
items.statement: Let F/F0 be unramified and p odd. Unitary chart (Lemma 4.3): (i) g′ ∈ U(V_n)°(F0) is regular semisimple for U(V_{n−1})-conjugation iff r(g′) ∈ (U(V_{n−1})×V_{n−1})(F0) is regular semisimple. (ii) If g′ ∈ U(V_n)°(F0)_srs, then for all but finitely many ξ ∈ F^1, ξg′ ∈ U(V_n)°(F0) and r_ξ(g′) = r(ξg′) is srs. (iii) If (g,u) ∈ (U(V_{n−1})×V_{n−1})(F0)_srs and det(1−g) ≠ 0, then for all but finitely many e ∈ u(1)(F0), (g,u,e) ∈ (U(V_{n−1})×V_{n−1}×u(1))°(F0) and r̃^{−1}(g,u,e) ∈ U(V_n)°(F0)_srs. Linear chart (Lemma 4.9): the same statements with S_n°, r(γ′) in (i) (equivalently r_ξ(γ′) for any ξ with ξγ′ ∈ S_n°), and det(1−γ) ≠ 0 added in (iii). The same holds with r♮.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Part (iii) (both Lemma 4.3(iii) and Lemma 4.9(iii)) is false without det(1−g) ≠ 0 (resp. det(1−γ) ≠ 0). The target open set requires it, and it does not depend on e. Counterexample: (g,u) = (1,u), u ≠ 0, in U(V_1)×V_1 is srs, yet (1,u,e) is never in the open set. Part (i) of the linear lemma should use r(γ′) (E7). The item's 'Starting with strongly regular data … inverse lifts are strongly regular for all but finitely many … e' inherits the missing hypothesis. Review note: Both uses of (iii), in the proofs of Proposition 4.12(i) and Theorem 5.5, first rescale by ξ so that det(1−g) ∈ O_F^×, so they are unaffected. The proof of (ii) checks out: R = gcd(P,Q) divides the separable det(λ+g′); the pencil P+tQ with gcd 1 has only finitely many branch values in characteristic 0; and t = ξ/(1−dξ) is injective in ξ.
items.proofOutline: Use triangular cyclic-span comparison and the characteristic-zero P+tQ pencil after removing its squarefree gcd. Six-way atomic splitting remains a completion gate.

items.name: RZ graph pullback
items.statement: If 1−d is an OF-unit, (δ×δ)*Γg′=Γg∩π2*Z(u). For u≠0 the corresponding derived pullbacks have no higher Tor and factor through the graph and divisor classes.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Add the paper's hypothesis g′ ∈ U(V_n)°(F0). The Tor vanishing uses Lemma B.2 (items 137–138) with regular ambient N_n × N_n and intersection of the expected dimension (Z(u) a relative divisor).
items.proofOutline: Solve the off-diagonal lifting equations between two possibly different deformations using the unit denominator. Check expected dimension and local complete intersections before AppendixB.2.

items.name: Derived rank reduction
items.statement: Under the unit-denominator hypothesis with r(g′)=(g,u), u≠0, the derived class Δ∩L(id×g′)Δ equals LNg∩LZ(u). For relative regular semisimple g′, Int(g′)=Int(g,u).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Apply derived associativity to the two Cartesian squares, Lemma4.4 and the projection formula. Unit rescaling of the special vector does not change its divisor.

items.name: Linear Cayley chart
items.statement: Write γ′ = (a b; c d) ∈ S_n (F^n = F^{n−1} ⊕ F u0), y′ = c^{−1}(γ′) = (1+γ′)(1−γ′)^{−1} = (y b̃; c̃ e) ∈ s_n and γ = c(y) = −(1−y)(1+y)^{−1} ∈ S_{n−1}. Then γ = a + (1−d)^{−1}bc, b̃ = 2(1−d)^{−1}(1−γ)^{−1}b, c̃ = 2(1−d)^{−1}c(1−γ)^{−1}, and γb̄ = ε_d b with ε_d = (1−d̄)/(1−d). Define r(γ′) = (γ, (b̃/√ε, (c̃/√ε)(1−y²)^{−1})) and r♮(γ′) = (γ, (b̃/√ε, c̃/√ε)); both lie in S_{n−1} × V′_{n−1} because conj(b̃) = −b̃, conj(c̃) = −c̃ and y² ∈ M_{n−1}(F0). With S_n° = {1−d ≠ 0, det(1−γ′) ≠ 0} and (S_{n−1}×V′_{n−1}×s_1)° = {det(1−γ) ≠ 0, det(1+y′) ≠ 0}, the map r̃ = (r, e): S_n° → (S_{n−1}×V′_{n−1}×s_1)° is a GL_{n−1}-equivariant isomorphism, and likewise for r♮ (Lemma 4.8). Set r_ξ(γ′) = r(ξγ′) for ξ ∈ F^1 (4.20).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: (4.17) prints the wrong sign for c̃: the correct formula is c̃ = +2(1−d)^{−1}c(1−γ)^{−1}, and the proof's two displayed equations also have sign errors (new misprint). 'Retaining the … c̃ sign' must not retain the printed sign. The definition of r in (4.18) takes c̃ as the lower-left block of y′ = c^{−1}(γ′), so r itself is unaffected. Naming: r♮, not r♭.
api: Construct inverse and invariant transport; visually recheck all barred formulas before Lean transcription.
unitTests: n=2 scalar block case; row/column variance and determinant identity.

items.name: Cayley matching
items.statement: Let γ′ ∈ S_n(F0)_srs and g′ ∈ U(V_n)(F0)_srs match, and let ξ ∈ F^1 satisfy ξγ′ ∈ S_n°; equivalently ξg′ ∈ U(V_n)°, since matching elements share d and the characteristic polynomial. Then r_ξ(γ′) and r_ξ(g′) are regular semisimple and match, and so are r♮_ξ(γ′) and r♮_ξ(g′). They are srs iff the characteristic polynomial of their first component is separable; by Lemmas 4.3(ii) and 4.9(ii) this holds for all but finitely many ξ.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Resolves the extraction's open gate: the printed srs annotations in Lemma 4.10 are false in general. There is an explicit γ′ ∈ S_3°(Q_3)_srs with r(γ′) = (γ,u′) and γ = −(1 i; 0 1) non-semisimple (new error below). Matching holds for the regular semisimple images; they are srs exactly when the common characteristic polynomial of the first component is separable, which holds for all but finitely many ξ. Review note: Proposition 4.12 is unaffected: it first chooses ξ by Lemma 4.3 so that r(g′) is srs, and srs is preserved by matching.
items.proofOutline: Use the same block F-conjugacy on the Lie matrices and the (1−x²)⁻¹ row correction. The printed unconditional srs target annotations remain an investigation gate.

items.name: Orbital rank reduction
items.statement: For a norm-one ξ with 1−ξd and det(1−ξγ′) units, the raw group unit orbital integral equals the semi-Lie unit integral for every s. Transferred values/derivatives require the separate factor comparison.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Statement faithful. The proof misprints det(1+y) = (1−d)^{−1}det(1−γ′); the correct value is 2^{n−1}(1−d)det(1−γ′)^{−1} (new misprint; both are units under (4.21), so the proof is unaffected). The transfer-factor comparison the paper cites from [37, Lem. 11.9] is proposed below as its own item, with a verified formula.
items.proofOutline: Identify integral orbit conditions and Haar quotients; import RSZ[37] Lemma11.9 for the transfer factor.

items.name: AFL rank equivalence
items.statement: Let F/F0 be an unramified quadratic extension of p-adic fields, p odd, and q the residue cardinality of F0. If q ≥ n, Conjecture 3.8(a) for V_n (for S_n) implies Conjecture 3.8(b) for V_{n−1}. If q ≥ n+1, Conjecture 3.8(b) for V_{n−1} implies Conjecture 3.8(a) for V_n. (Proposition 4.12(i) asserts the equivalence for q ≥ n; the printed proof of the second implication fails at q = n.)
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The paper states an equivalence for q ≥ n. Its proof of (b) for V_{n−1} ⇒ (a) for V_n needs ξ ∈ F^1 with det(1−ξg′) ∈ O_F^× and 1−ξd ∈ O_F^×. With q + 1 = n + 1 norm-one residue classes, such ξ need not exist, and the claim 'otherwise both sides of (a) vanish' used to force 1−d ∈ O_F^× is unproved (new gap). The printed argument proves this direction for q ≥ n+1. Review note: The derivative comparison also needs ω(γ′) = ω(r(γ′)) (cited to [37, Lem. 11.9]): proposed as a new item with a verified proof.
items.proofOutline: Choose among q+1 norm-one residue classes avoiding at most n eigenvalues, then a generic lift; combine orbital and derived-intersection rank reductions.

items.name: AFL norm-unit reduction
items.statement: Under Proposition4.12's hypotheses, group AFL for Sn−1 implies semi-Lie AFL in dimension n−1 for vectors of unit norm.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Faithful. The orbital identity is 'left to the reader' in the paper. It is routine: for u2u1 ∈ O_{F0}^×, GL_{n−1}(O_{F0}) acts transitively on integral pairs with that product, the stabiliser is GL_{n−2}, and ω(γ,u′) equals the S_{n−1} transfer factor with e ↔ u1.
items.proofOutline: Split off the unit vector and identify the derived graph intersection with the lower-rank group model; verify the bound independently of part(i).

items.name: Vertex lattices and Deligne–Lusztig strata
items.statement: For the nonsplit unramified Hermitian space, vertex lattices satisfy Λ⊂Λ∨⊂ϖ⁻¹Λ with odd type t=dim(Λ∨/Λ). The closed stratum VΛ in Nred is smooth projective of dimension (t−1)/2; the reduced space is stratified by these loci.
items.locator: §5.1 (Bruhat–Tits stratification), p. 896, citing [42] and [24, §2.2] ([26] is cited only for Lemma 5.1)
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct containment incidence, strata and group transport; export finite orbit types.
unitTests: Type1 strata have dimension zero; maximum dimension is floor((n−1)/2).

items.name: Stratum-cycle intersection is locally constant
items.statement: Let n ≥ 3 and let Λ ⊂ V_n be a vertex lattice of maximal type, t(Λ) = 2⌊(n−1)/2⌋ + 1. For C ∈ Ch_{1,V(Λ)}(N_{n,red}) (Q-coefficients), the function Int_C(u) = χ(N_n, C ⊗^L O_{Z(u)}) on V_n∖{0} is locally constant and compactly supported, and it is constant on U∖{0} for some neighbourhood U of 0.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: 'a maximal vertex lattice' is ambiguous and could invert the meaning. A lattice maximal under inclusion has minimal type. The paper requires a vertex lattice of maximal type, t(Λ) = 2⌊(n−1)/2⌋+1.
items.proofOutline: Reduce curve classes to type3 strata and apply Li–Zhang[26] Corollary6.2.2. A higher-dimensional replacement in Remark5.3 avoids unproved formal Adams multiplicativity.

items.name: Fixed-g local constancy
items.statement: For full-group regular semisimple g, Int(g,u) is locally constant on vectors making (g,u) regular semisimple.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Faithful; g is regular semisimple in the sense that F[g] is étale of degree n. Checked the proof: the lattice span{g^i u} is locally constant in u, N^g ∩ Z(u) = N^g ∩ Z(span), 0-dimensional classes pair to 0 with a Cartier divisor, and for horizontal C, Tor_1 vanishes against a Cartier divisor. Remark 5.3's (B.3)-free route needs Lemma 5.1 in all dimensions ([26, §6.4]); proposed as a new item.
items.proofOutline: The lattice OF{g^i u} and intersection support stabilize locally. Represent the derived class by curves, handle vertical curves with Lemma5.1 and horizontal curves by normalization and Tor vanishing. Use Remark5.3's alternative if formal (B.3) is unavailable.

items.name: Characteristic-polynomial submersion
items.statement: Fix (g0,u0,e0) ∈ (U(V_n)×V_n×u(1))°(F0) with g′ = r̃^{−1}(g0,u0,e0) ∈ U(V_{n+1})(F0)_srs. With g0 held fixed, the map (u,e) ↦ charpoly(r̃^{−1}(g0,u,e)) ∈ (U(V_{n+1})//U(V_{n+1}))(F0), defined on an open neighbourhood of (u0,e0) in V_n × u(1), is submersive at (u0,e0).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The item lets the Cayley coordinate g vary, which makes it a weaker claim than the paper's. In Lemma 5.4, g0 is fixed and only (u,e) vary; this is what Theorem 5.5 needs. Also, the printed proof uses 'regular semi-simplicity of x0', which the hypothesis does not give (new gap, easily closed; see issues).
items.proofOutline: Pass to Lie invariants char(x), e and u*x^j u, decompose the étale algebra, and show the norm differential is surjective. Record the exact analytic opens and tangent maps before implementation.

items.name: Joint local constancy of Int
items.statement: The function (g,u)↦Int(g,u) is locally constant on (U(Vn)×Vn)srs.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: The proof invokes the ξ-rescaling from the proof of Proposition 4.12(i) (making det(1−ξg) a unit), which needs q + 1 > n. Theorem 5.5 is stated for every odd p (new gap). Its only use (§15, F0 = Q_p, p ≥ n) satisfies q ≥ n. For general q, the statement is supplied by Mihatsch [32] (Local constancy of intersection numbers, Algebra Number Theory 16 (2022), 505–519), whose result Mihatsch–Zhang describe as local constancy on the whole regular semisimple locus.
items.proofOutline: Lift to a strongly regular rank-(n+1) element, hold its conjugacy class fixed via Lemma5.4, and use fixed-g local constancy plus derived rank reduction. Audit any use of Proposition4.12's cardinality bound.

items.name: Compact support modulo conjugation
items.statement: The support of Int on the strongly regular semi-Lie locus is compact modulo U(Vn).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Faithful. The proof needs [24, Prop. 4.1] and transitivity of U(V_n)(F0) on vertex lattices of a given type; proposed as a new item.
items.proofOutline: A point in the intersection determines a minimal closed DL stratum with gΛ=Λ and u∈Λ. Finitely many vertex types give a finite union of compact KΛ×Λ representatives.

items.name: Unitary Shimura datum with CM torus
items.statement: For CM F/F0 and dimension n, take a CM type Φ and strict fake Drinfeld signature rφ0=n−1, rφ=n elsewhere in Φ. Construct GQ of rational similitudes and G̃=ZQ×GmGQ≅ZQ×ResF0/Q U(V), with reflex field E=EΦEr containing F.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct h(z), reflex field and product-level comparison; retain the positive CM-torus convention.
unitTests: Only the distinguished real place has signature(n−1,1).

items.name: Integral level and bad-prime data
items.statement: D0 includes residual characteristic2, primes ramified in F/F0 and inert nonsplit V; D is a rational-prime pullback containing D0 and d its rational product. Away d choose self-dual Λv and hyperspecial KG,v; choose KZ maximal away d and small level at d.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct localization, adelic level factors and self-dual choices; prove independence under allowed conjugacy.
unitTests: A nonsplit place cannot be excluded from d while retaining hyperspecial self-dual data.

items.name: Auxiliary CM moduli
items.statement: M0(S), for S in (LNSch)/O_{EΦ}, is the groupoid of (A0, ι0, λ0): A0 an abelian scheme over S, ι0: O_F → End(A0) satisfying the Kottwitz condition char(ι0(a) | Lie A0) = ∏_{ϕ∈Φ}(T − ϕ(a)) for all a ∈ O_F (6.7), and λ0 a principal polarization whose Rosati involution induces the Galois involution on O_F; morphisms are O_F-linear isomorphisms pulling back λ0′ to λ0. M0 is a Deligne–Mumford stack, finite and étale over Spec O_{EΦ} ([18, Prop. 3.1.2]). Its generic fibre is a disjoint union of copies of Sh_{K°_{ZQ}}(ZQ, {h_{ZQ}}) ([40, Lem. 3.4]). The paper assumes F/F0 ramified at some finite place, so that M0 ≠ ∅ ([40, Rem. 3.5(ii)]), fixes one copy, and adds a K_{ZQ}-level structure η0 only at the primes dividing d (M0,K_{ZQ}; [30, §C.3]).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The finite étale property of M0 over O_{EΦ} ([18, Prop. 3.1.2]) is unconditional; the standing assumption that F/F0 is ramified (p. 903, via [40, Rem. 3.5(ii)]) only ensures that M0 is nonempty. The item's 'under the paper's nonemptiness convention' reads as a hypothesis of finite étaleness, and the defining conditions (Kottwitz condition (6.7), Rosati involution = Galois involution) are not stated.
api: Define the CM groupoid, component selection and level; compare its generic fibre with the torus canonical model.
unitTests: Do not infer nonemptiness from a formal moduli definition.

items.name: RSZ integral unitary moduli
items.statement: Definition 6.1 (p. 904–905). For S in (LNSch)/O_E[1/d], M_{K_G̃}(G̃)(S) is the groupoid of (A0,ι0,λ0,η0,A,ι,λ,η) with (A0,ι0,λ0,η0) ∈ M0,K_{ZQ}(S); A an abelian scheme; ι: O_F[1/d] → End(A)⊗Z[1/d] satisfying the Kottwitz condition of signature ((n−1,1)_{ϕ0}, (n,0)_{ϕ∈Φ∖{ϕ0}}); λ: A → A^∨ a prime-to-d principal polarization whose Rosati involution induces the Galois involution on O_F[1/d]; η a ∏_{v|d}K_{G,v}-orbit of π1(S,s)-stable isometries of hermitian F_d-modules V_d(A0,A) = ∏_{p|d}Hom_{F⊗Q_p}(V_p(A0),V_p(A)) ⥲ V(F_{0,d}) (6.10)–(6.12); and the Eisenstein condition of [39, §5.2] at every place w ∤ d of F (automatic unless w is ramified over p; footnote 2). Morphisms: an isomorphism of (A0,ι0,λ0,η0) in M0,K_{ZQ}(S) and an O_F-linear d-isogeny A → A′ (invertible in Hom(A,A′)⊗Z[1/d]) pulling back λ′ to λ and η′ to η. Generic version (6.13) over E: F-action, polarization, and a K_G-orbit of isometries V̂(A0,A) ⥲ V(A_{F0,f}).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Omits two defining conditions: the Rosati involution of λ must induce the Galois involution on O_F[1/d], and η must be π1(S,s)-stable. The morphisms are also not given: an isomorphism of the CM data and an O_F-linear d-quasi-isogeny (an invertible element of Hom(A,A′)⊗Z[1/d]) pulling back λ′ and η′.
api: Define objects and d-isogeny morphisms, π1-invariant level sheaves and base change; compare all-primes generic Tate level.
unitTests: Unramified F/F0 does not make the F0/Qp Eisenstein condition redundant.

items.name: RSZ smooth integral model
items.statement: The moduli in Definition6.1 is separated, finite type and smooth DM of relative dimension n−1 over OE[1/d]; sufficiently small level at d gives a smooth quasi-projective scheme, assumed thereafter.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Verify RSZ[40] Theorem5.2 and[39] Theorem6.2 under the stated sign/Eisenstein conditions; generic comparison is with the canonical Shimura model.

items.name: Generic global KR divisors
items.statement: For ξ∈F0,+ and KG-orbit µ in V(A0,f), Z(ξ,µ) classifies the generic moduli point with u∈HomF°(A0,A), h(u,u)=ξ and η(u)∈µ. Weighted Z(ξ,φ) is the finite compact-support sum of proper pushforward divisor classes.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Correct morphisms to u′∘a0=ϕ∘u for the CM-source isomorphism a0 and ϕ:A→A′; define pushforward with multiplicities.
unitTests: The printed u∘ϕ is not type-correct.

items.name: Integral global KR divisors
items.statement: Over OE[1/d] require u∈HomOF(A0,A)⊗Z[1/d], fixed positive norm and KG,d-level orbit. For φ=1Λ^d⊗φd define the weighted integral divisor; its generic fibre is the corresponding generic weighted divisor.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct integral liftability, corrected morphisms, finite orbit sums and generic-fibre compatibility.
unitTests: Nonintegral special Hom outside d does not define an integral point.

items.name: KR forgetful map
items.statement: The KR forgetful morphism is representable, finite and unramified.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Apply KR[25] Proposition2.9 or Liu[30] Proposition4.22 with the actual base and level; retain finite pushforward multiplicities.

items.name: Flat Cartier KR divisors
items.statement: Étale locally on the ambient RSZ model, the KR morphism defines a Cartier divisor, flat over OE[1/d].
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Import BHKRY[5] §2.5 and Liu[30] Proposition4.22; distinguish a finite unramified divisor map from a globally embedded divisor.

items.name: Basic-locus p-adic uniformization
items.statement: At ν∤d over inert v0, the completed RSZ model is the quotient of the relative unitary RZ space times the away-v0 level cosets by the nearby global unitary group, with the CM-torus component factor as in (7.3)–(7.6).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Verify absolute-to-relative RZ comparison via Mihatsch[31] Theorem3.1 and its Eisenstein condition; identify the CM-torus partition and each fibre's quotient.

items.name: Formal KR orbit expansion
items.statement: For positive ξ the pullback of Z(ξ,φ) to each CM-torus component of the basic completion is the finite sum over G′(F0)-orbits of (u,g) of φ^v0(g⁻¹u)[Z(u)×1gK^v0].
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Transport the special Hom through uniformization and descend the equivariant orbit sum; verify finiteness and multiplicities, not just equality of supports.

items.name: Nonmaximal CM order
items.statement: Let α be irreducible, conjugate reciprocal and integral away d. Put F′=F[T]/α, extend conjugation by T↦T⁻¹, and explicitly assume F′ is CM over its totally real fixed field F0′. Set Rα=OF[1/d][T]/α and Ram(α) its nonmaximal-order places outside d.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct involution and local order, maximality test and finite bad set; the CM assumption is independent.
unitTests: The reciprocal polynomial T²−3T+1 alone fails the totally-real assertion.

items.name: Naive and twisted fat CM moduli
items.statement: CM(α,g) parametrizes integral RSZ objects with ϕ∈EndOF(A)⊗Z[1/d], α(ϕ)=0, ϕ*λ=λ, and level intertwining by g∈G(F0,d). CM(α) is g=1. The order may be nonmaximal and no extra CM signature is imposed.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Observation for the design job: under the smallness assumption the paper imposes from p. 905 on (M is a scheme), the untwisted CM(α) = CM(α,1) is empty for irreducible α of degree n ≥ 2. For g ∈ K_{G,d} the ϕ in Definition 7.6 is an automorphism of the object (id on A0, ϕ on A: it is a d-quasi-isogeny since ϕ^{-1} = ϕ^† ∈ End(A)⊗Z[1/d], it preserves λ and η), and objects of a scheme-valued moduli problem have no automorphism but the identity; then α(1) = 0, which is impossible. So only the twisted CM(α,g), g ∉ K_{G,d}, carry content: Remark 7.7's 'large dimensional components' concerns them, and the weighted cycle (7.16) only needs them. Status missing, route UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles: agreed.
api: Construct forgetful map and double-coset dependence; retain potentially higher-dimensional special fibres.
unitTests: Do not identify the naive fat cycle with a finite-flat curve at bad-order primes.

items.name: Fat CM finite forgetful morphism
items.statement: Proposition 7.9(a) (p. 911). Let α ∈ A_n(O_{F0}[1/d]) be irreducible over F (with F′ CM, §7.4) and g ∈ G(F_{0,d}). Then CM(α,g) → M is representable, finite and unramified.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The item does not say where g lives. The paper prints 'g ∈ ∏_{v|d} G(F_v)', a misprint for g ∈ G(F_{0,d}) = ∏_{v|d}G(F_{0,v}) as in Definition 7.8 (new issue below).
items.proofOutline: Use bounded endomorphisms, rigidity, Hilbert representability and the abelian-scheme valuative criterion; expand the finite-type argument rather than using α(ϕ)=0 alone without polarization.

items.name: Fat CM properness and good-order étaleness
items.statement: Proposition 7.9(b), corrected (p. 911). CM(α,g) → Spec O_E[1/d] is proper, hence finite by (a). Its generic fibre is finite étale over E (it is zero-dimensional and unramified in characteristic 0). The paper's claim of finite étaleness over Spec O_E[1/d] ∖ Ram(α) holds at most above the places v ∉ Ram(α) where F′/F is unramified, where the Lie-type of the O_{F′}-action is locally constant and the rigidity argument of [18, Prop. 3.1.2(3)] can run; that restricted version would need its own proof. It fails in general above places where F′/F ramifies (counterexample in the new issue).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The second clause is false as printed (new issue below). CM(α,g) need not be étale over O_E[1/d] above a place v ∉ Ram(α) at which F′/F is ramified: the generic fibre contains points whose residue fields are ramified there over E. The later sections use only properness and the zero-dimensional generic fibre (§9.1).
items.proofOutline: Exclude a nonzero toric degeneration using the CM action's degree; apply formal CM deformation theory when the local order is maximal.

items.name: Rational characteristic polynomial
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over any field and rational endomorphism ϕ, det(T−ϕ|Vℓ A) lies in Q[T], has degree2dim A and is independent of ℓ≠char(k).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Recover the polynomial from deg(m−ϕ) for rational m. Supply the degree polynomial and quasi-endomorphism extension.

items.name: F-linear characteristic polynomial
items.statement: With F-action and F-linear rational ϕ, its rank-n characteristic polynomial on Vℓ A lies in F[T] and is independent of ℓ.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Recover F-valued traces using the nondegenerate trace pairing and the Q-traces of ι(a)ϕ^j; use Newton identities in characteristic zero.

items.name: Characteristic polynomial in connected families
items.statement: For an abelian scheme over a connected locally noetherian base, the rational characteristic polynomial of a quasi-endomorphism is constant; the F-linear polynomial is likewise constant when the F-action is present.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Use the lisse Tate sheaf where ℓ is invertible and cover the base using two distinct primes. Split the Q/F variants into separate nodes at final atomization.

items.name: Hecke correspondence and fixed locus
items.statement: For g∈G(F0,d), Hk[KgK] classifies two RSZ objects with common CM factor and a polarized d-quasi-isogeny intertwining level by g. Its map to M×M is finite, each projection finite étale. Its fixed locus is the fibre product with the diagonal.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct both projections, finite correspondence and diagonal fixed functor; expose source/target quasi-isogeny direction.
unitTests: g=1 gives the identity-level correspondence, not arbitrary automorphisms.

items.name: Characteristic decomposition of fixed Hecke loci
items.statement: The Hecke fixed locus has a finite open-and-closed decomposition by F-characteristic polynomial. Each occurring polynomial is conjugate reciprocal and integral away d; for irreducible α its fibre is CM(α,g).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Use connected-family constancy and finite type; prove integrality on Tate modules or Dieudonné modules in characteristic ℓ, and use Cayley–Hamilton plus irreducibility for α(ϕ)=0 iff charFϕ=α.

items.name: Derived CM cycle
items.statement: LCM(α,g) is [OHk⊗L OΔ] restricted to the open-and-closed CM(α,g) support, a rational supported G0-class. Weighted LCM(α,φ0) is the finite double-coset sum for φ0=1K^d⊗φ0,d.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Define restriction in support K-theory, weighted sum, and finite pushforward; do not replace the derived class by OCM.
unitTests: Nonmaximal-order higher-dimensional support must still permit a virtual one-cycle.

items.name: Virtual dimension of derived CM
items.statement: LCM(α,g) lies in the dimension≤1 filtration F1G0(CM(α,g)) because the diagonal is regular of codimension n−1 and the correspondence is finite étale over M.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Proof note for the design job. Footnote 5's 'apply (B.3) to the image' only controls the pushforward of the class to M×M (or to M). That pushforward is all §9.1 uses, but it does not give (7.15) on CM(α,g) itself. A complete argument: Lπ*O_Δ, for π: Hk → M×M, is the pullback of the Koszul class of the regular immersion Δ, of Adams weight ≥ n−1 (items 132, 133). Pullback preserves the weight decomposition, and Hk is regular of pure dimension n (finite étale over M), so F^{n−1}K_0^{CM}(Hk)_Q = F_1K′_0(CM(α,g))_Q (Appendix B, item 131). The inclusion holds only with Q-coefficients.
items.proofOutline: Use scheme supported rational K-filtration multiplicativity, then dimension-preserving finite pushforward. Expand the footnote's finite-image argument; do not import the unproved formal analogue of (B.3).

items.name: Formal Hecke uniformization
items.statement: On each basic CM-torus component, the completed Hecke correspondence is the nearby-group quotient of the RZ diagonal times the discrete away-v0 Hecke pair correspondence.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Apply the uniformization functor to the quasi-isogeny and identify both projection maps; retain the double-coset condition g1⁻¹g2∈KgK.

items.name: Naive CM uniformization
items.statement: Proposition 7.17(i) and its twisted form (p. 917–918). Let α ∈ A_n(O_{F0}[1/d]) be irreducible over F, ν ∤ d a place of E over an inert v0, and G′ the nearby unitary group at v0. For g ∈ G(F_{0,d}), the restriction of the formal completion CM^(α,g) to each fibre of (7.5) is the disjoint union of the descended cycles [N^δ_{O_Ĕν} × 1_{hK^{v0}_G}] over (δ,h) ∈ G′(F0)\(G′(α)(F0) × G(A^{v0}_{0,f})/K^{v0}_G) with h^{-1}δh ∈ K^{v0,d}_G × K_{G,d} g K_{G,d}. The printed statement is the case g ∈ K_{G,d}, where both sides are empty under the smallness assumption.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: As printed, (i) is about CM(α) = CM(α,1), which is empty under the standing smallness assumption (see item 53), and its index set gives no points: a δ with h^{-1}δh ∈ K^{v0}_G and N^δ ≠ ∅ lies in a compact subgroup at every place, so it is torsion, hence 1 for neat K_{G,d}. The content the proof supports, and which (ii) needs summand by summand, is the twisted version.
items.proofOutline: Use rigidity of quasi-isogenies and the equality of the action on the away-v0 coset to identify δ with the global endomorphism.

items.name: Derived CM uniformization
items.statement: The completed weighted derived CM class is the orbit sum φ0^v0(h⁻¹δh)[LNδ×1hK] on each CM-torus component.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Lift the naive comparison to derived graph-diagonal tensor products with flat base change. The semiglobal variant allows arbitrary away-v0 level but needs its own model comparison.

items.name: Chow-valued special-divisor generating series
items.statement: Set Z(0,φ)=−φ(0)c1(ω). The adelic generating series sums Z(ξ,ω(hf)φ)Wξ^(n)(h∞) over totally positive ξ and the zero term, in CH1 of the generic unitary Shimura variety.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct the zero coefficient, Weil action and coefficient-valued q-expansion.
unitTests: Do not omit the negative Hodge-bundle constant term.

items.name: Chow modularity
items.statement: The preceding Chow-valued series is a holomorphic SL2 automorphic form of parallel weight n and level fixing φ, with the stated algebraic coefficient structure, over totally real F0.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Import orthogonal Borcherds/Yuan–Zhang–Zhang modularity, the unitary embedding trick of Liu[28], and the CM-torus component comparison. This does not prove integral arithmetic modularity for general F0.

items.name: Complex KR uniformization
items.statement: At a complex embedding ν of E, use the nearby Hermitian space indefinite only at its real restriction and the negative-line domain D. Each CM-torus component is G′(F0)\(D×G(Af)/K); positive-norm u gives D_u of negative lines perpendicular to u.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct the component and divisor quotients; compare with formal uniformization.
unitTests: The negative-line domain is empty for a positive-definite Hermitian space.

items.name: Complex KR orbit expansion
items.statement: For positive ξ, the complex divisor is the weighted descended sum φ(g⁻¹u)[D_u×1gK] over rational unitary orbits; it can be regrouped by stabilizer double cosets.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Transport special Homs through complex uniformization, descend with multiplicities, and apply orbit-stabilizer regrouping. Correct the component-projection cross-reference.

items.name: Kudla Green function
items.statement: §8.3 (8.9)–(8.13), pp. 921–922. Let V′ be the archimedean nearby hermitian space at v0 and D = D_{v0} the negative C-lines in V′⊗_{F,w0}C. For u ∈ V′(F0) and z ∈ D with basis z̃: R(u,z) := ⟨u_z,u_z⟩ = |⟨u,z̃⟩|²/⟨z̃,z̃⟩ ≤ 0. Ei(−r) := −∫_r^∞ e^{−t}t^{−1}dt for r > 0. For h∞ with Iwasawa parameter a_{v0} (1.6) and u ≠ 0 (any norm, including null), Kudla's Green function is GK(u,h∞)(z) = −Ei(4πa_{v0}R(u,z)) on D ∖ D_u (Kudla's −Ei(−2πaR_K) with R_K = −(u_z,u_z)_{tr} = −2R(u,z); the paper prints 2π). Also GK(0,h∞) := −log a_{v0}. For ξ ∈ F0, GK(ξ,h∞,φ) := Σ_{(u,g) ∈ V′_ξ(F0) × G(A_{0,f})/K_G} φ(g^{-1}u)·(GK(u,h∞) × 1_{gK_G}), G′(F0)-invariant, descending to the fibre (8.5); for ξ ∈ F_{0,+} it is a Green function for Z(ξ,φ)⊗_{E,ν}C ([28, Prop. 4.9]).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: (1) The formula |h(u,z̃)|²/h(z̃,z̃) is right, but the paper prints ⟨u,z̃⟩² in (8.9), a misprint recorded below. (2) The Green function is stated as −Ei(2πa_v R(u,z)). The normalization matching the q^ξ = e^{2πiξτ} generating series (8.2), (8.14), (8.17) and Kudla's function (used by [8] for Theorem 8.4) is −Ei(4πa_{v0}R(u,z)) (new issue below). (3) The locator covers (8.13), but the statement omits the descended function GK(ξ,h∞,φ) and its Green-function property.
api: Construct orthogonal projection, logarithmic singularity and descended orbit sum; preserve the parameter a_v.
unitTests: Changing the basis z̃ leaves R unchanged.
For a negative Hermitian line, R(u,z)=−|u|².

items.name: Automorphic Green function and correction
items.statement: §8.3 (8.14), p. 922. For ξ ∈ F_{0,+} and φ ∈ S(V(A_{0,f})), GB(ξ,φ) is the automorphic (Bruinier/Oda–Tsuzuki) Green function of Z(ξ,φ), normalized as in [5, §7.3]. Set GB(ξ,φ) := 0 for ξ ∉ F_{0,+}, including ξ = 0. The metrized Hodge term −φ(0)ĉ1(ω̂) cancels between Kudla's and Bruinier's constant terms and enters only through Int(0,Φ); this is the convention the proof of Proposition 14.5 (p. 964) uses. Then Z_{v0,corr}(h,φ) := Σ_{ξ∈F0}(GK(ξ,h∞,ω(h_f)φ) − GB(ξ,ω(h_f)φ))·W^{(n)}_ξ(h∞), which depends on the archimedean place v0.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The statement says GB comes 'with its source-prescribed zero/nonpositive extensions', but the paper prescribes none. It introduces GB(ξ,φ) only for ξ ∈ F_{0,+} (p. 922) and still sums (8.14) over all ξ ∈ F0 (gap recorded below). The convention the later proof uses must be stated.
api: Import an actual normalized Green function, not an arbitrary function satisfying modularity.
Close the source's omitted nonpositive-coefficient conventions before implementation.
unitTests: The difference must be smooth at a positive divisor after identical singular parts cancel.

items.name: Green-comparison modularity
items.statement: For F0=Q, the correction series evaluated at any complex Shimura point belongs to Aexp of weight n and Weil-stabilizer level.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Theorem 8.4 is quoted from Ehlen–Sankaran [8, Th. 3.6 and proof of Th. 4.13], where Kudla's Green function is normalized for the q^ξ series. With (8.11) as printed (−Ei(2πaR)) that source does not apply. The item must be read with GK = −Ei(4πa_{v0}R), as Mihatsch–Zhang do ((3.15) and (6.4)); see the new issue on (8.11). The ξ ∉ F_{0,+} convention of item 71 is also needed. Status missing: agreed (gate G4).
items.proofOutline: Import Ehlen–Sankaran[8] Theorem3.6 and its unitary comparison in the proof of Theorem4.13. The totally real extension is later work, not assumed here.

items.name: Localized arithmetic divisor group
items.statement: For a regular flat arithmetic model over OE with finitely many places S removed, use Q-divisors plus compatible Green functions modulo (div f,−log|f|²). Removing S is quotienting by the classes supported above S.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Status missing with a source route to ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights:R35.1: acceptable, but R35.1 as described in the atlas plans hermitian bundles and arithmetic degree over arithmetic curves only. This item needs Ĉh^1 of a regular, flat, non-proper model of arbitrary dimension over O_E∖S, Green functions with log-log growth ([7]), and the pairing with proper 1-cycles ([3, §2.3]). The source route must extend R35.1's scope explicitly, or name GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.2, which covers only surfaces. Otherwise the item stays unowned.
api: Construct principal relations, vertical localization and pullback to proper arithmetic curves; use the same arithmetic-degree normalization as other height roadmaps.
unitTests: Over Q, a vertical p-fibre corresponds to (0,2log p).

items.name: Arithmetic KR series
items.statement: Equip positive KR divisors with GB; define the zero coefficient as −φ(0)c1(ω̂), with Petersson-metrized automorphic line bundle. Form the q-series in localized arithmetic CH1.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct arithmetic classes and level-dependent q-expansions; import generic metrized degree rather than duplicate it.
unitTests: The zero coefficient uses the metric, not just the algebraic line bundle.

items.name: Arithmetic KR modularity over Q
items.statement: For F0=Q, the arithmetic series is holomorphic of weight n on Γ(N), with prime factors of N among the inverted primes, in the stated rational/algebraic coefficient space.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Adapt BHKRY[5] TheoremB's Borcherds-divisor calculation from maximal level to the localized smooth model. This adaptation and source hypotheses remain an external closure obligation.

items.name: Proper-cycle arithmetic pairing
items.statement: Pair arithmetic CH1 with proper one-cycles on a regular flat arithmetic model, quotienting only vertical cycles rationally equivalent to zero on proper special-fibre subschemes. Over OE\S the value lies in R_S=R/spanQ{log p:S has a place above p}.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Status missing with a source route to ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights:R35.1: acceptable, but R35.1 as described in the atlas plans hermitian bundles and arithmetic degree over arithmetic curves only. This item needs Ĉh^1 of a regular, flat, non-proper model of arbitrary dimension over O_E∖S, Green functions with log-log growth ([7]), and the pairing with proper 1-cycles ([3, §2.3]). The source route must extend R35.1's scope explicitly, or name GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.2, which covers only surfaces. Otherwise the item stays unowned.
api: Construct proper-curve degree and vertical rational-equivalence descent; retain archimedean and residue-degree factors.
unitTests: Inverting a new prime enlarges the quotient of R by its logarithm.

items.name: Derived CM class as a proper one-cycle
items.statement: Push F1G0(CM) to supported G0(M), pass to gr1, identify it rationally with CH1 supported on the CM image, and map to the proper-cycle quotient. Properness and zero-dimensional generic fibre are required.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct the filtration-preserving finite pushforward and cycle-class map; share the K-to-Chow comparison with SchemeKTheoryOperations.
unitTests: Discarding F0 is legitimate only for this one-cycle target, not for arbitrary K-classes.

items.name: Normalized arithmetic intersection series
items.statement: For Φ=φ0⊗φ, standard away d, set Int(τ,Φ)=(ẐB(τ,φ),LCM(α,φ0))/(τ(ZQ)[E:F]), where τ(ZQ)=#ZQ(Q)\ZQ(Af)/KZ. Its zero coefficient is the negative metrized Hodge pairing times φ(0).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct the component normalization, coefficientwise pairing and R_S-valued series.
unitTests: The CM-torus component count and [E:F] must each be divided out exactly once.

items.name: Intersection-series modularity
items.statement: For F0=Q, Int(τ,Φ) is holomorphic of weight n and the specified level, with coefficients in R_S⊗Q Qbar.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Apply the proper-cycle pairing linearly to Theorem8.6; justify coefficient extension and finite-dimensional modular-form representation.

items.name: No generic intersection
items.statement: For irreducible α and nonzero ξ, the KR divisor and fat CM cycle do not intersect the generic fibre.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Use irreducibility to make the special vector cyclic and apply the CM action to contradict the characteristic-zero signature; compare RSZ[40] Theorem8.5.

items.name: No good split intersection
items.statement: Outside the bad set S with standard local test functions, a place split in F/F0 contributes no special-fibre intersection.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Apply the split local Hom/signature obstruction from RSZ; deduce Int_v(ξ,Φ)=0.

items.name: Good inert support is basic
items.statement: Outside S, at an inert place the intersection support is contained in the basic locus.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Use the cyclic CM action to force the relevant isocrystal to be basic. Do not uniformize the whole model as if every point were basic.

items.name: Local arithmetic intersection decomposition
items.statement: §9.3 (9.11)–(9.16), p. 927. For ξ ∈ F_{0,+} (so that, by Theorem 9.2(i), Ẑ_B(ξ,φ) and LCM(α,φ0) do not meet on the generic fibre), Int(ξ,Φ) = Σ_{v0} Int_{v0}(ξ,Φ) with Int_{v0}(ξ,Φ) := (τ(ZQ)[E:F])^{-1} Σ_{ν|v0} Int♮_ν(ξ,Φ). For finite ν, Int♮_ν = ⟨Ẑ_B(ξ,φ), LCM(α,φ0)⟩_ν·log q_ν: the Euler–Poincaré characteristic of the derived tensor product on M⊗O_{E,(ν)}, with q_ν the residue cardinality. For a complex place ν, Int♮_ν = ⟨GB_ν(ξ,φ), LCM(α,φ0)_{ν,C}⟩, the Green function summed over the complex 0-cycle and counted once (½Σ over the two embeddings in ν). Hence Int(τ,Φ) = Int(0,Φ) + Σ_{v0} Int_{v0}(τ,Φ) with Int_{v0}(τ,Φ) := Σ_{ξ∈F_{0,+}} Int_{v0}(ξ,Φ)q^ξ.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: It repeats the paper's weight 'log q_ν = 2' for complex places. With the Gillet–Soulé normalization of §8.4 (principal divisors (div f, −log|f|²), so V_p = (0, 2 log p)), a complex place contributes the Green-function value once (½ per complex embedding). With weight 2, (9.14) fails and Theorem 10.1 is off by a factor 2 (new issue below). The unit test 'A complex place carries factor 2' is wrong for the same reason.
api: Construct local terms and finite support; isolate zero coefficient from the positive series.
unitTests: A complex place carries factor2; a finite extension scales length with ramification.

items.name: Inert local orbit formula
items.statement: Theorem 9.4 (p. 928). Let v0 ∤ d be a place of F0 inert in F, w0 | v0, ξ ∈ F_{0,+}, and Φ = Φ_{v0} ⊗ Φ^{v0} with Φ_{v0} = 1_{K°_{G,v0}} ⊗ 1_{Λ°_{v0}}. Then Int_{v0}(ξ,Φ) = 2 log q_{v0} Σ_{(δ,u) ∈ [(G′(α)×V′_ξ)(F0)]} Int_{v0}(δ,u)·Orb((δ,u),Φ^{v0}). Here G′ = U(V′) is the unitary group of the nearby space at v0; Int_{v0}(δ,u) is the intersection number (3.13) of the semi-Lie AFL for F_{w0}/F_{0,v0} at the image of (δ,u) in (U(V′)×V′)(F_{0,v0}); and Orb((δ,u),Φ^{v0}) = ∏_{v≠v0} Orb((δ,u),Φ_v), each defined by (2.15) with the Haar measure on G(F_{0,v}) normalized by vol(K_{G,v}) = 1.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the normalization fixing Orb. The paper takes the product of local orbital integrals (2.15) with Haar measures on G(F_{0,v}) such that vol(K_{G,v}) = 1, and this is what makes the double-coset count in the proof equal Orb. It also omits that Int_{v0}(δ,u) is the semi-Lie AFL intersection number (3.13) for F_{w0}/F_{0,v0}.
items.proofOutline: Apply both formal orbit expansions, multiply the RZ length by base-change degree, sum CM components, and use Σν|w[Eν:Fw]=[E:F]. The factor2 comes from q_w=q_v².

items.name: Archimedean fixed point and orbit formula
items.statement: For δ of irreducible CM characteristic α in the nearby group, there is a unique fixed negative line zδ, and no nonzero rational u is perpendicular to it. The normalized archimedean Kudla intersection is the rational-orbit sum GK(u,h∞)(zδ)Orb((δ,u),Φ).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Theorem 10.1 as printed is correct for the Gillet–Soulé weight (value counted once per complex place). With the printed definitions (9.12)/(10.1)–(10.2) (log q_ν = 2), the left side is 2Σ GK(u,h∞)(z_δ)·Orb (new issue). The finite-place orbital integrals use vol(K_{G,v}) = 1 as in Theorem 9.4, and the fixed point z_δ exists because F′ is CM (§7.4 standing assumption): the eigenvalues of δ have absolute value 1, so its eigenlines are nondegenerate and mutually orthogonal. Status missing: agreed.
items.proofOutline: Diagonalize the CM action orthogonally; signature singles out the negative eigenline. If u is perpendicular, all δ^i u are, contradicting cyclicity.

items.name: Refined CM Hermitian invariant
items.statement: The δ-action identifies V with restriction of scalars of a one-dimensional F′/F0′-Hermitian space W whose trace form is V. Define ξ′=q′(u)∈F0′ with TrF0′/F0 ξ′=ξ. The unique negative real embedding v′ gives R(u,zδ)=−|ξ′|v′.
