items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct the trace-form equivalence and refined orbit invariant; relate conjugacy to ker(H1(T)→H1(G)).
unitTests: A single negative embedding, not merely negative total trace, controls the archimedean derivative.

items.name: Archimedean exponential-integral formula
items.statement: Corollary 10.3, corrected (p. 931). Under the assumptions of Theorem 10.1, with GK(u,h∞)(z) = −Ei(4πa_{v0}R(u,z)), Int^K_{v0}(ξ,Φ) = −Σ_{(δ,u)} Ei(−4πa_{v0}|ξ′|_{v′0})·Orb((δ,u),Φ). The sum runs over G′(F0)-orbits in (G′(α)×V′_ξ)(F0), ξ′ = q′(u) ∈ F′0 is the refined invariant (10.6) with tr_{F′0/F0}ξ′ = ξ, and v′0 | v0 is the unique real place of F′0 where ξ′ < 0 (terms with no such place vanish). In the paper's printed normalization (−Ei(2πaR)), the same holds with 2π in place of 4π, and (10.8) is its a_{v0} = 1 specialization.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The item rightly retains a_v (E27) but keeps the paper's Ei argument 2π. With Kudla's normalization of the Green function (new issue on (8.11); Mihatsch–Zhang (6.4) and (6.12)), the archimedean formula has 4π. The printed (10.8) is the a_{v0} = 1 case of the paper's own 2π normalization.
items.proofOutline: Insert the projection invariant into GK and the orbit formula. The parameter omission must not be propagated to the full adelic function.

items.name: Paired Green correction is modular
items.statement: For F0=Q, IntK−B(h,Φ), obtained by pairing the Green correction with the generic CM cycle and dividing by τ(ZQ)[E:F], is in Aexp of weight n and fixed Weil level; no integral model is needed for this correction.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Apply Theorem8.4 at each CM point and sum with multiplicities; justify the finite generic CM support.

items.name: Even-dimensional Weil representation
items.statement: For a nondegenerate even-dimensional quadratic space over the global base field, construct O(V)(A)×SL2(A) on Schwartz functions. Locally m(a) acts by χV(a)|a|^(d/2)φ(ax), n(b) by ψ(bq(x))φ(x), and w by γV times self-dual positive-sign Fourier transform, χV(a)=(a,(−1)^(d/2)det V).
items.locator: §11.1, (11.1) and the definitions of χ_V, det(V), γ_{V_v} and the Fourier transform that follow, pp. 932–933
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Planned by MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.2 (generator formulas, Weil index) and MP.4 (adelic Weil representation); fine. In even dimension the SL2 action is linear. For the owner: det(V) is the determinant of the Gram matrix ½(⟨x_i,x_j⟩), and γ_{V_v} is a fourth root of unity because dim V is even.
api: Prove generator relations, orthogonal-sum and character changes, and splitting to SL2 in even dimension.
unitTests: For Hermitian rank n the real dimension is 2n and m(√a) contributes a^(n/2).

items.name: Theta convergence and rational invariance
items.statement: Let (V,q) be a nondegenerate quadratic space of even dimension d over a global field F, and let φ ∈ S(V(A_F)). For (g,h) ∈ O(V)(A_F) × SL2(A_F), the sum θ_φ(g,h) = Σ_{ξ∈V(F)} ω(g,h)φ(ξ) converges absolutely, and θ_φ is left invariant under O(V)(F) × SL2(F).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The item states no setting. V is a nondegenerate even-dimensional quadratic space over a global field F, and φ ∈ S(V(A_F)). Review note: Planned by MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.5 (theta series, convergence, rational invariance by Poisson summation); fine. The paper asserts this without proof.
items.proofOutline: Use adelic Schwartz estimates, lattice discreteness and Poisson summation; prove local uniform convergence for differentiation.

items.name: Partially linearized automorphic kernel
items.statement: For affine X with reductive G-action and quadratic G-module V, fix a semisimple quotient fibre X(α). Define KΦ,α(g,h)=Σ(x,u)∈(X(α)×V)(F)ω(h)Φ(g⁻¹·(x,u)); its G(F)-quotient integral is SL2(F)-invariant when absolutely convergent.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct partial Weil action commuting with G and the kernel; attach convergence predicates before integration.
unitTests: Archimedean general Schwartz functions are not assumed finite sums of pure tensors.

items.name: Unitary regular and singular orbit terms
items.statement: Let F/F0 be a CM extension, V an n-dimensional F/F0-hermitian space, and G = U(V), acting on G × V by g·(δ,u) = (gδg^{−1}, gu). Let α ∈ A_n(F0) be irreducible over F. Then (δ,u) ∈ (G(α)×V)(F0) is regular semisimple if and only if u ≠ 0. For Φ ∈ S((G×V)(A0)) and regular semisimple (δ,u), define Orb((δ,u),Φ) := ∫_{G(A0)} Φ(g^{−1}·(δ,u)) dg (11.5). For δ ∈ G(α)(F0), define Orb((δ,0),Φ) := vol(G_δ(F0)\G_δ(A0)) ∫_{G_δ(A0)\G(A0)} Φ(g^{−1}·δ, 0) dg (11.6), where the centralizer G_δ is an anisotropic F0-torus. The kernel integral J(h,Φ) of (11.3) then splits as in (11.4) into two parts. The u = 0 part is Σ_{δ∈[G(α)(F0)]} Orb((δ,0), ω(h)Φ) (11.7), and only finitely many of its terms are nonzero, uniformly in h ∈ H(A0). The u ≠ 0 part is the sum over [(G(α)×V)(F0)]_rs of Orb((δ,u), ω(h)Φ).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the definition (11.5) of the regular global orbital integral and the finiteness claim of (11.7). The setting is also left implicit: G = U(V) for an n-dimensional hermitian space V over a CM extension F/F0, and α ∈ A_n(F0) irreducible over F.
api: Construct stabilizer measures, unfolding and finite singular support.
unitTests: Do not integrate the u=0 term over G(A) as if its stabilizer were trivial.

items.name: Unitary orbital-sum convergence
items.statement: (a) For every Φ ∈ S((G×V)(A0)), Σ_{(δ,u)∈[(G×V)(F0)]_rs} ∫_{G(A0)} |Φ(g^{−1}·(δ,u))| dg < ∞; in particular the same holds for the sum over [(G(α)×V)(F0)]_rs. (b) Suppose Φ is K∞-finite for K∞ = ∏_{v|∞} SO(2,R) ⊂ H(F0,∞), acting by the Weil representation (H = SL_{2,F0}). Then the sum defining J(h,Φ) converges absolutely and uniformly for h in compact subsets of H(A0). Hence h ↦ J(h,Φ) is smooth on H(A0) and left invariant under H(F0).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Part (b) also asserts that h ↦ J(h,Φ) is left invariant under H(F0); the item omits this. Also, K∞ = ∏_{v|∞} SO(2,R) ⊂ H(F0,∞) acts through the Weil representation, and part (a) holds for arbitrary Φ, not only pure tensors. Review note: Missing; routed to the Jacquet–Rallis Part II (route 9). The proof rests on Beuzart-Plessis [1, Prop. A.1.1(ii),(iii),(v),(vii)], which no item covers (see coverage).
items.proofOutline: Use the regular quotient torsor, algebraic height bounds, discriminant control and the product formula to reduce to a convergent rational-height sum. Apply the same estimates to derivatives; split the two assertions at final atomization.

items.name: Unitary Fourier orbit expansion
items.statement: Let Φ ∈ S((G×V)(A0)) have K∞-finite archimedean component. Then J(h,Φ) = Σ_{(δ,u)∈[(G(α)×V)(F0)]} Orb((δ,u), ω(h)Φ) (11.15), where the u = 0 terms are those of (11.6). For ξ ∈ F0^×, the ξ-th Fourier coefficient (1.12) of h ↦ J(h,Φ) is Σ_{(δ,u)∈[(G(α)×V_ξ)(F0)]} Orb((δ,u), ω(h)Φ) (11.16), where V_ξ = {q(u) = ξ}.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the hypothesis of (11.16) that Φ_∞ is K∞-finite, which is needed so that Lemma 11.1(b) applies. The Fourier coefficient is a function of h, as in (1.12).
items.proofOutline: Use absolute convergence to interchange integrations and sums, then additive-character orthogonality.

items.name: Linear nilpotent orbit decomposition
items.statement: Let V0 = F0^n (columns) and V0* (rows), and let V′ = V0 × V0* with q(u1,u2) = u2(u1), so that ⟨u′,u′⟩ = 2q(u′). Let G′ = GL(V0) act on V′ by (std, std^∨) and on S_n by conjugation, and let α ∈ A_n(F0) be irreducible over F. Then (S_n(α) × V′)(F0) has exactly three G′(F0)-orbits that are not regular semisimple. They consist of the pairs (γ,u′) with u′ = (0,0), with u′ ∈ 0+ = {(u1,0) : u1 ≠ 0}, or with u′ ∈ 0− = {(0,u2) : u2 ≠ 0}. The last two orbits have trivial stabilizers. For Φ′ ∈ S((S_n×V′)(A0)), regular semisimple (γ,u′) and s ∈ C, define Orb((γ,u′),Φ′,s) = ∫_{G′(A0)} Φ′(g^{−1}·(γ,u′)) |det g|^s η(g) dg (11.19), where η = η_{F/F0}∘det; it is the product of the local integrals (11.20). The integral J(h,Φ′,s) = ∫_{[G′]} Σ_{(γ,u′)} r(g)ω(h)Φ′(γ,u′) |det g|^s η(g) dg is defined as J(h,Φ′,s)_0 + J(h,Φ′,s)_rs (11.21), with J_rs = Σ_{[(S_n(α)×V′)(F0)]_rs} Orb((γ,u′), ω(h)Φ′, s). The orbit of (0,0) is discarded because η is nontrivial on its stabilizer. J_0 is the regularized sum over 0± defined in §12.6.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The locator covers (11.19)–(11.21), but the item states neither the linear orbital integrals (11.19)–(11.20), the decomposition (11.21), nor the action. §11.4 lets G′ act on V′ by (std, std^∨), whereas §12.5 uses the inverse action for n = 1; see the new issue on action conventions.
api: Construct split quadratic form q(u1,u2)=u2u1, orbit classification and J_s's separated terms.
unitTests: q(u′)=0 alone is not equivalent to being in a nilpotent orbit when the refined invariant can have trace zero.

items.name: Linear regular-orbit convergence
items.statement: The regular rational-orbit sum of absolute linear orbital integrals converges locally uniformly for complex s; with K∞-finite Φ′ it is locally uniform in (h,s), and derivatives in s are justified.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Statement acceptable. Two remarks. In (a), |det g|^s means |det g|^{Re s}. 'Derivatives in s are justified' is a consequence (by Weierstrass, locally uniform limits of holomorphic functions), not part of the lemma. The paper proves the lemma only by 'the same argument as Lemma 11.1'. The extra factor |det g|^{Re s} needs ‖g‖ ≪ (‖g·x‖‖x‖)^c on the regular semisimple torsor, which the norm item proposed under coverage must supply.
items.proofOutline: Adapt the discriminant-height estimates, absorbing |det g|^Re(s) and logarithmic derivative factors uniformly on compact s-sets.

items.name: Corrected Gaussian and partial Gaussian transfer
items.statement: Work over C/R with ψ(x) = e^{2πix}. (i) Let V be a positive-definite n-dimensional hermitian space, with q(u) = ⟨u,u⟩, and let G = U(V) with vol(G(R)) = 1. The Gaussian test function is Φ_V(g,u) = 1_{G(R)}(g) e^{−2πq(u)} (corrected; the paper prints e^{−π⟨u,u⟩}). (ii) A function Φ′ ∈ S((S_n×V′_n)(R)) is a Gaussian test function if it is a transfer of the tuple {Φ_V}, where Φ_V is as in (i) for the positive-definite V and Φ_V = 0 for every other isometry class. The paper only expects these to exist. (iii) T_n ⊂ S_n(R) is the set of diagonal elements (≅ U(1)^n), and T_n^rs is the subset with distinct entries. Let Ω ⊂ T_n^rs be compact. Φ′ is a partial Gaussian test function relative to Ω if two conditions hold for every regular semisimple (γ,u′) ∈ Ω × V′. If (γ,u′) matches (δ,u) ∈ (U(V)×V)(R) with V positive definite, then Orb((γ,u′),Φ′) = Orb((δ,u),Φ_V) = e^{−2πq(u)}. If (γ,u′) matches an orbit in a non-positive-definite space, then Orb((γ,u′),Φ′) = 0. Here Orb((γ,u′),Φ′) = ω(γ,u′)·Orb((γ,u′),Φ′,0) includes the transfer factor. (iv) In rank one, V′ = R×R with q(x,y) = xy, and the corrected linear function is φ′(x,y) = ½(x+y)e^{−π(x²+y²)} (the paper prints 2^{−3/2}(x+y)e^{−π(x²+y²)/2}).
items.locator: §12.1 (12.1)–(12.2), p. 940; §12.2 Definitions 12.1–12.2, pp. 940–941; §12.3 (12.6), p. 941. Functions corrected by Mihatsch–Zhang, J. Eur. Math. Soc. (DOI 10.4171/JEMS/1375), §7.2 (7.6) and footnote 5, p. 48, and §7.3, p. 49
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The item compresses Definitions 12.1–12.2. It omits the compact Cartan subspace T_n, the normalization vol(G(R)) = 1, and the fact that the special values in (12.5) include the transfer factor ω(γ,u′); see the new issue on Lemma 12.6. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Checked independently. With ψ(b) = e^{2πib} and q(u) = ⟨u,u⟩ (1.4), the Weil representation sends e^{−2πq} to χ_n(κθ)a^{n/2}e^{2πiq(u)(b+ia)}, the weight-n vector matching W_ξ (1.5); the printed e^{−π⟨u,u⟩} is not. For φ′(x,y) = ½(x+y)e^{−π(x²+y²)} on V′ = R² with q = xy: for ξ > 0, Orb((1,ξ),φ′) = ∫_0^∞(1+ξ/t²)e^{−π(t²+ξ²/t²)}dt, and the substitution w = t − ξ/t gives ∫_R e^{−π(w²+2ξ)}dw = e^{−2πξ}, the corrected Gaussian's orbital integral. For ξ < 0 the substitution w = t + |ξ|/t gives 0. Writing x = (X+Y)/√2, y = (X−Y)/√2, φ′ ∝ X e^{−π(X²+Y²)} for q = (X²−Y²)/2: weight 3/2 − 1/2 = 1. Equivalently, φ′_new(x,y) = φ′_old(√2x,√2y), so Orb_new(ξ) = Orb_old(2ξ) and ∂Orb_new(ξ) = ½e^{−2πξ}Ei(−4π|ξ|) for ξ < 0, consistent with E15. Definition 12.2's partial-matching condition is transcribed correctly. Status missing, route JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison: agreed. | REPAIR VERDICT: sound. With ψ(t) = e^{2πit}, the pairing xy′+x′y and the self-dual measure dx dy, e^{−π(x²+y²)} is Fourier-fixed; e^{−π(x²+y²)/2} is not, and goes to 2e^{−2π(x²+y²)}. In coordinates with q = (s²−t²)/2, (x+y)e^{−π(x²+y²)} = √2·s·e^{−π(s²+t²)}, which has weight 3/2 − 1/2 = 1. The corrected rank-one orbital value is e^{−2πξ} = e^{−2πq(u)}, which I checked numerically. Status missing, routed to the Jacquet–Rallis Part II (route 9); fine.
api: Keep full Gaussian transfer, whose existence is only expected here, separate from the partial construction.
Implement the published scaling correction before checking weight or q-expansion.
unitTests: The old Gaussian is not a weight-one vector for the stated ψ.
For ξ>0 the corrected rank-one orbital value is exp(−2πξ).

items.name: Bessel and exponential-integral kernels
items.statement: For c > 0 and s ∈ C, let K_s(c) = ½∫_0^∞ e^{−c(u+u^{−1})/2} u^s du/u. Then K_s(c) is entire in s, K_{−s} = K_s, and K_{1/2}(c) = √(π/2) e^{−c} c^{−1/2}. For y > 0, d/ds|_{s=1/2} K_s(y) = −√(π/2) e^{y} y^{−1/2} Ei(−2y), where Ei(−r) = −∫_r^∞ e^{−t} dt/t for r > 0.
items.locator: §12.3: definition before Lemma 12.3, p. 942, and the identity in the proof of Lemma 12.3, p. 943 (cited from [35]); Ei from (8.10)
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The statement names 'the source's order derivative' but does not state it. The identity used is d/ds|_{s=1/2} K_s(y) = −√(π/2) e^{y} y^{−1/2} Ei(−2y) for y > 0, cited from [35], with Ei as in (8.10). Review note: Missing: neither library has Bessel K or Ei at the pinned commits (git grep at Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474). Routed with AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors (AL.0, parameter integrals); fine. I checked the order-derivative identity numerically at y = 0.8 (15 digits).
api: Construct holomorphic dependence on the order, differentiation bounds and Ei comparison.

items.name: Corrected rank-one orbital integral
items.statement: Let φ′(x,y) = ½(x+y)e^{−π(x²+y²)} and Orb((1,ξ),φ′,s) = ∫_{R^×} φ′(t^{−1}, tξ)|t|^s sgn(t) d^×t, as in (2.14). For ξ ∈ R^×, Orb((1,ξ),φ′,s) = |ξ|^{(1−s)/2}[K_{(1−s)/2}(2π|ξ|) + sgn(ξ)K_{(−1−s)/2}(2π|ξ|)]. The transfer factor at (1,ξ) is 1. So Orb((1,ξ),φ′) = e^{−2πξ} for ξ > 0 and 0 for ξ < 0, and for ξ < 0, ∂Orb((1,ξ),φ′) = ½e^{−2πξ}Ei(−4π|ξ|). In the convention of (12.14), replace s by −s; the derivative then changes sign.
items.locator: §12.3, Lemma 12.3 and Remark 12.4, pp. 942–943; Bessel orders as in the proof's last display (E14); Gaussian rescaled per Mihatsch–Zhang §7.2 (E12)
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Correct, but the s-convention should be stated. This is the convention of (2.14), with integrand t^{−s}; it is opposite to that of (12.14)–(12.15) (new issue on action conventions). The values at s = 0 include the transfer factor, which is 1 at (1,ξ) (Remark 12.4). Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. I checked the derivation by hand (substitute t ↦ |ξ|^{1/2}t, then u = t²). Numerically it agrees with quadrature at ξ = ±0.7, 1.9 and −1.3 and s = 0.3 and −0.45, to 12 digits; the value at s = 0 and the derivative ½e^{−2πξ}Ei(−4π|ξ|) (ξ < 0) also agree.
items.proofOutline: Substitute t=exp y in the real multiplicative integral, then t² into the Bessel integral. Correct the statement's swapped Bessel orders and use the later Gaussian scaling. Numerical checks accompany, but do not prove, the formulas.

items.name: Corrected rank-one Weil action
items.statement: Let h = n(b)m(a^{1/2})κθ with a > 0, b ∈ R, and let ξ ∈ R^×. The corrected φ′ is a χ1-eigenvector of SO(2,R). In the (2.14) convention, Orb((1,ξ),ω(h)φ′,s) = χ1(κθ)e^{2πiξb}·a·|ξ|^{(1−s)/2}[K_{(1−s)/2}(2πa|ξ|) + sgn(ξ)K_{(−1−s)/2}(2πa|ξ|)]. Hence Orb((1,ξ),ω(h)φ′) = χ1(κθ)a^{1/2}e^{2πiξ(b+ia)} for ξ > 0 and 0 for ξ < 0. For ξ < 0, ∂Orb((1,ξ),ω(h)φ′) = ½χ1(κθ)a^{1/2}e^{2πiξ(b+ia)}Ei(−4πa|ξ|).
items.locator: §12.3, Lemma 12.5, p. 943; corrected per Mihatsch–Zhang Proposition 7.4, (7.7), p. 48
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The formula follows from (11.1): n(b) multiplies the orbit q = ξ by e^{2πiξb}, and m(a^{1/2}) contributes a^{1/2}·a^{s/2}·Orb((1,aξ),φ′,s). Combined with item 99, this gives the displayed formula, which agrees with Mihatsch–Zhang (7.7). The weight-one property holds only for the corrected φ′ (E12).
items.proofOutline: Apply the three Weil generators to the corrected φ′, then the rank-one integral. Preserve phase, κ-weight and negative ξ; do not reuse the printed old phase formulas.

items.name: Partial Gaussian descent chart
items.statement: Write G′(R) = GL_n(R) = ANK, with A ≅ (R^×)^n diagonal, N upper unipotent and K = SO(n). Normalize ∫_{G′(R)} f(g)dg = ∫_A∫_N∫_K f(ank) da dn dk, with da = ∏ dt_i/|t_i|. Let Ω ⊂ T_n^rs be compact, and let U ⊃ Ω be an open subset of T_n^rs that meets each orbit of the permutation group S_n at most once; in the application Ω is a small neighbourhood of one point. Then (h,t,u′) ↦ (h^{−1}th, h^{−1}·u′), from NK × U × V′ to S_n × V′, is a K∩A-torsor onto an open subset, where ε ∈ K∩A acts by ε·(h,t,u′) = (εh, t, ε·u′). Choose the following. ϕ_N ∈ C_c^∞(N) with ∫ϕ_N = 1 and ϕ_N(εnε^{−1}) = ϕ_N(n) for ε ∈ K∩A. ϕ_K = 1_K/vol(K). ϕ_{T_n} ∈ C_c^∞(U) with ϕ_{T_n}(t) = η̃(det(t)^{−⌊n/2⌋}∏_{i<j}(t_j − t_i))^{−1} for t ∈ Ω, where η̃ is the fixed extension of sgn to C^×. φ′ = ∏_{i=1}^n ½(x_i+y_i)e^{−π(x_i²+y_i²)} on V′ = (R×R)^n. Then Ψ = ϕ_N⊗ϕ_K⊗ϕ_{T_n}⊗φ′ is K∩A-invariant, descends to a Schwartz function on the open image, and extends by zero to Φ′ ∈ S((S_n×V′)(R)).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The item diagnoses the defect but states no construction. Each fibre of NK × T_n^rs → S_n^{c,rs}, (h,t) ↦ h^{−1}th, has n!·2^{n−1} points: one K∩A-orbit for each permutation of the entries of t. The map (12.9) must be (h,t,u′) ↦ (h^{−1}th, h^{−1}·u′) for the action used in the proof of Lemma 12.6. The N-cutoff must be invariant under conjugation by K∩A (E17), and ϕ_{T_n} must carry the transfer-factor phase (new issue on Lemma 12.6). The Haar measure is ∫_{G′(R)} f = ∫_A∫_N∫_K f(ank): the product measure pushed forward along the 2^{n−1}-to-1 multiplication map, which is what the proof of Lemma 12.6 uses. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound as a diagnosis, incomplete as a construction. The n = 2 fibre example is right: with t = diag(1,i), t′ = diag(i,1) and k = [[0,1],[−1,0]], k^{−1}t′k = t. The construction becomes complete once the conditions above are stated. The Iwasawa decomposition is planned in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/LieGroups (layer 9) and ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.4; the descent itself is new, and belongs to the Jacquet–Rallis Part II.
api: Replace the descent by genuine local slices or a proved Weyl-compatible pushforward, with correct multiplicities, sign character and Haar Jacobian.
Prove the constructed function is Schwartz and has the required orbital integral; this is an explicit open gate.
unitTests: A cutoff that is1 at t and0 at t′ does not descend through that fibre.

items.name: Partial Gaussian orbital factorization, conditional on repaired construction
items.statement: Let Φ′ be constructed as in the repaired item 101. For γ ∈ Ω and every regular semisimple (γ,u′), the local integral (11.20) is Orb((γ,u′),Φ′,s) = ϕ_{T_n}(γ)·∫_A φ′(a^{−1}·u′)|det a|^s η(a) da, and the A-integral is the product of the n rank-one integrals of item 99 at the points (x_i,y_i). Consequently, for γ ∈ Ω, Orb((γ,u′),Φ′) = e^{−2πq(u)} when (γ,u′) matches (δ,u) in the positive-definite space, and 0 when it matches an orbit in a non-positive-definite space. So Φ′ is a partial Gaussian test function relative to Ω. The same factorization holds for the regular nilpotent orbits (γ,0±), with the Tate regularization (12.18)/(12.27) (Remark 12.7).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The factorization is right. Two points need stating. The factorization should be stated for the raw integrals at every s. The partial-Gaussian conclusion holds only after the transfer-factor phase is built into ϕ_{T_n}: with the printed ϕ_{T_n}|_Ω = 1, one gets Orb((γ,u′),Φ′) = η̃(det(γ)^{−⌊n/2⌋}∏_{i<j}(t_j − t_i))·e^{−2πq(u)}. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound, conditional on the repaired construction of item 101. The word 'normalized' in the statement should name the transfer-factor phase (new issue on Lemma 12.6); without it the partial-Gaussian clause is false for n ≥ 2.
items.proofOutline: Integrate N and K with normalized cutoffs, then factor over the diagonal torus. The source's chart proof is not accepted until the descent gate in item101 is closed.

items.name: Rank-one regularized global distribution
items.statement: Let n = 1 and V′ = F0 × F0 with q(u1,u2) = u1u2, and let G′ = GL1 act by g·(u1,u2) = (g^{−1}u1, gu2). Let η = η_{F/F0} for a CM extension F/F0, and let φ′ ∈ S(V′(A0)). Define J(φ′,s) = Orb(0+,φ′,s) + Orb(0−,φ′,s) + Σ_{ξ=q(u′)∈F0^×} Orb(u′,φ′,s) (12.20), with one rational orbit for each ξ ≠ 0, where the terms are as follows. Orb(u′,φ′,s) = ∫_{A0^×} φ′(g^{−1}·u′)|g|^sη(g)dg. Orb(0+,φ′,s) = ∫_{A0^×} φ′(g,0)|g|^sη(g)dg = L(s,η)∏_v Orb(0+,φ′_v,s), with Orb(0+,φ′_v,s) = ∫_{F_{0,v}^×} φ′_v(g,0)|g|_v^sη_v(g)dg / L(s,η_v). Orb(0−,φ′,s) = ∫_{A0^×} φ′(0,g)|g|^{−s}η(g)dg = L(−s,η)∏_v Orb(0−,φ′_v,−s). Each term is continued analytically in s. The orbit {(0,0)} contributes 0, because η is nontrivial on its stabilizer. Put J(h,φ′,s) = J(ω(h)φ′,s).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The item should state the formulas and the action it uses. §12.5 identifies G′ = GL1 acting by g·(u1,u2) = (g^{−1}u1, gu2), the inverse of §11.4's (std, std^∨) action. With this action, Orb(0+,φ′,s) = ∫φ′(g,0)|g|^sη(g)dg and Orb(0−,φ′,s) = ∫φ′(0,g)|g|^{−s}η(g)dg.
api: Construct analytic continuation of the two nilpotent terms and retain the ±s convention.
unitTests: Do not interpret the initially divergent full theta integral as an ordinary convergent integral.

items.name: Normalized Tate factors
items.statement: For local Schwartz data, the Tate zeta integral divided by its L-factor extends to an entire function; at finite places it is a Laurent polynomial in q^s, and standard unramified data gives1. For nontrivial global η the completed global L-function is entire.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Planned by AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1, which covers Tate integrals, normalization by L, the unramified computation and global continuation. For nontrivial η the completed L(s,η) is entire; AL.1 keeps the poles of the trivial character, so this item specializes it. Fine.
items.proofOutline: Use the exact local/global Tate theorem, preserving the trivial-character poles in the general API and specializing only after nontriviality is proved.

items.name: Rank-one regularized modularity
items.statement: J(ω(h)φ′,s) is smooth in h, entire in s, and left SL2(F0)-invariant.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Statement faithful; the setting (CM F/F0, η = η_{F/F0}) is that of item 103. Proof note: smoothness in h is taken from Lemma 11.2(b), which assumes K∞-finite data, while the theorem is stated for every φ′; see the new issue on Theorem 12.9. It is true in general by continuity of ω on the Schwartz space.
items.proofOutline: Prove upper-triangular invariance directly. For the Weyl element use Poisson, partial Fourier transform, integrate first over compact norm-one ideles to kill the zero orbit, apply Tate's functional equation in a convergent half-plane, then continue analytically.

items.name: Corrected Gaussian nilpotent factor
items.statement: Let v | ∞ and φ′_v(x,y) = ½(x+y)e^{−π(x²+y²)}. In the convention of §12.5, the normalized local nilpotent integral (12.18) is Orb(0+,φ′_v,s) = ∫_{R^×} φ′_v(g,0)|g|^s sgn(g) d^×g / (π^{−(s+1)/2}Γ((s+1)/2)) = ½. For h = n(b)m(a^{1/2})κθ, Orb(0+,ω(h)φ′_v,s) = ½χ1(κθ)a^{(1−s)/2}. (The printed φ′ gives 2^{s/2−1}.)
items.locator: §12.5, Lemma 12.11, pp. 948–949; Gaussian corrected per Mihatsch–Zhang (7.6)
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. It follows from ∫_0^∞ e^{−πx²}x^{s+1}dx/x = ½π^{−(s+1)/2}Γ((s+1)/2), which I checked numerically at s = 0.4 and 1.3; the printed φ′ reproduces 2^{s/2−1}. The dependence on a uses ω(m(a^{1/2}))φ′(x,0) = a^{1/2}φ′(a^{1/2}x,0); n(b) acts trivially on q = 0.
items.proofOutline: Evaluate the signed real Gaussian Mellin integral divided by ΓR(s+1). The old function gives2^(s/2−1); scaling changes this to½.

items.name: Rank-one reduction over the CM fixed field
items.statement: For irreducible compact α, Sn(α)(F0) is one GLn-orbit with centralizer ResF0′/F0 Gm. The vector and covector become rank-one F0′ modules, with q=TrF0′/F0 q′; η∘det restricts to ηF′/F0′.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed.
api: Construct the centralizer, trace pairing and character norm compatibility; compactness is equivalent to the CM condition.
unitTests: Distinguish F0′-norm zero from trace-zero q.

items.name: Higher-rank nilpotent continuation
items.statement: Fix γ ∈ S_n(α)(F0). For each v | ∞, let Φ′_v be the partial Gaussian test function of §12.4, relative to a compact neighbourhood of γ. For every place v, the integral in (12.27) converges absolutely for Re(s) > 0, and Orb((γ,0+),Φ′_v,s) extends to an entire function of s; for v nonarchimedean it is a Laurent polynomial in q_v^{−s}. The 0− integral behaves the same way with s replaced by −s. If Φ′ = ⊗_vΦ′_v with Φ′_v = 1_{(S_n×V′)(O_{F0,v})} for almost all v, then Orb((γ,0+),Φ′_v,s) = 1 for all but finitely many v (depending on γ and Φ′).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The item omits two things. First, the absolute convergence for Re(s) > 0; this holds for the action of §12.5 but fails for the (std, std^∨) action of §11.4 (new issue on action conventions). Second, the hypotheses of the 'almost all v' clause: a pure tensor Φ′ = ⊗Φ′_v (printed 'Φ = ⊗Φ_v'; new issue) with Φ′_v = 1_{(S_n×V′)(O_{F0,v})} for almost all v. Review note: Proof note on (12.28)–(12.30). 'A suitable choice of measure dg on Ω_v' should be a cutoff c ∈ C_c^∞(G′(F0,v)) with ∫_{T′(F0,v)} c(tg)dt = 1, not a compact subset. The right side of (12.30) is (12.18), not (12.19) (new issue). The a_i in (12.29) lie in C in general, and in Q when Φ′_v is Q-valued.
items.proofOutline: Integrate first over a compact centralizer quotient; express the result as finite Σaiλi^sφi and apply rank-one Tate theory over F0′. Check the quotient measure rather than treating a compact subset as a canonical transversal.

items.name: Higher-rank modularity of J_s
items.statement: Assume the following: γ ∈ S_n(α)(F0) is fixed, with F′/F0′ CM; Φ′ = ⊗_vΦ′_v, where for v | ∞, Φ′_v is the repaired partial Gaussian test function of §12.4 relative to a compact neighbourhood Ω_v of γ; and Φ′_v = 1_{(S_n×V′)(O_{F0,v})} for almost all v. Then (h,s) ↦ J(h,Φ′,s) = J_0 + J_rs is entire in s and left invariant under H(F0). More precisely, J(h,Φ′,s) = Σ_{i=1}^m a_iλ_i^s J^{F0′}(h,φ′_i,s) with a_i ∈ C and λ_i ∈ Q_+^×, where J^{F0′} is the rank-one distribution of item 103 for F′/F0′, restricted from SL2(A_{F0′}) to SL2(A0).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The theorem depends on the construction only through Lemma 12.6 at the archimedean places, which makes φ′_{v,s} independent of s there; the repair keeps this.
items.proofOutline: Reduce to finite combinations of rank-one regularized distributions over F0′, restricting SL2(A_F0′) to SL2(A_F0). This depends on the repaired Gaussian construction.

items.name: Special-value and derivative expansion
items.statement: Set J(h,Φ′) = J(h,Φ′,0) and ∂J(h,Φ′) = d/ds|_{s=0} J(h,Φ′,s). Set ∂Orb((γ,u′),Φ′_v) = d/ds|_{s=0} Orb((γ,u′),Φ′_v,s), where for 0± the local integrals are those of (12.27). Define ∂J_v(Φ′) = Σ_{(γ,u′), u′≠0} ∂Orb((γ,u′),Φ′_v)·Orb((γ,u′),Φ′^v), where for 0± the factor away from v is L(0,η′)∏_{w≠v}Orb((γ,0±),Φ′_w). Define ∂Orb(0+,Φ′) = L′(0,η′)∏_vOrb((γ,0+),Φ′_v,0) and ∂Orb(0−,Φ′) = −L′(0,η′)∏_vOrb((γ,0−),Φ′_v,0), where η′ = η_{F′/F0′} (the paper prints L(s,η); E18); ∂Orb(0±) is their sum (12.37). Then ∂J(h,Φ′) = ∂Orb(0±,ω(h)Φ′) + Σ_v ∂J_v(ω(h)Φ′) (12.38). Here the local 0− terms enter through s ↦ Orb((γ,0−),Φ′_v,−s), and the ξ-th Fourier coefficient of each ∂J_v is the corresponding sub-sum over V′_ξ.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Correct once E18 is applied. It should also say how the 0− term is differentiated. The local 0− factors enter as Orb((γ,0−),Φ′_v,−s), so their s-derivatives carry a minus sign in (12.36)–(12.38).
api: Construct coefficientwise derivative and local decomposition with finite/nonzero support estimates; distinguish raw and transferred local terms.
unitTests: The global product of transfer factors on a rational orbit is1.
Differentiate L(−s) as −L′(−s).

items.name: Holomorphic coherent analytic series
items.statement: Fix an irreducible α ∈ A_n(F0), with F0 totally real and F/F0 CM. Let Φ′ = ⊗_v Φ′_v ∈ S((S_n × V′_n)(A0)) be a pure tensor whose components at v | ∞ are the partial Gaussian test functions (in the corrected normalization, Mihatsch–Zhang (7.6)). Let Φ = ⊗_v Φ_v ∈ S((U(V) × V)(A0)), where V is an n-dimensional totally positive definite F/F0-Hermitian space and Φ_v is the Gaussian for v | ∞. Let K ⊂ SL2(A_{0,f}) be a compact open subgroup acting trivially on Φ and on Φ′. Then h ↦ J(h,Φ′) and h ↦ J(h,Φ) each lie in A_hol(H(A0),K,n). That is: each is left H(F0)-invariant, right K-invariant and of parallel weight n, and is holomorphic on H^{[F0:Q]} and at every cusp. For every h_f, J♭_{h_f}(τ,·) = Σ_{ξ∈F0, ξ≥0} A_ξ q^ξ, with A_ξ = 0 unless ξ lies in a fractional ideal depending on (Φ′_f, h_f) (resp. (Φ_f, h_f)).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Minor. Proposition 13.3 (p. 954) makes two separate assertions and does not need Φ and Φ′ to match: one for Φ′ (a pure tensor with partial Gaussian archimedean components, relative to the fixed irreducible α) and one for Φ (V n-dimensional and totally positive definite, Gaussian archimedean components). 'Fixed level' means one compact open K ⊂ SL2(A_{0,f}) fixing both. The proofOutline's 'nonnegative Fourier coefficients' is wrong wording: the proof shows that the ξ-th coefficient vanishes unless ξ ≥ 0 (totally semi-positive) and ξ lies in a fractional ideal. It says nothing about the sign of the coefficients. Review note: Missing; route 9 (JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison, Part II) is the right owner. The weight-n claim for J(·,Φ′) comes from Lemma 12.5, whose printed formulas are wrong (E15). It holds with Mihatsch–Zhang's corrected rank-one formulas (item 100). REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The only correction the item carries is the corrected Gaussian normalization (E12/E15), and Mihatsch–Zhang Proposition 7.4 with footnote 5 supports it.
items.proofOutline: Use modularity, corrected weight-n Gaussian eigenvectors, explicit nonnegative Fourier coefficients and nilpotent constants at every cusp.

items.name: Coherent comparison from lower-rank FL
items.statement: Theorem 13.4. Setting of §13.2: F0 totally real, F/F0 CM, α ∈ A_n(F0) irreducible with γ ∈ S_n(α)(F0) regular elliptic compact, and V an n-dimensional totally positive definite F/F0-Hermitian space. S is a finite set of non-archimedean places containing every place of residue characteristic 2 (and, implicitly, every finite place where the fixed global η̃ is ramified). Φ = ⊗Φ_v and Φ′ = ⊗Φ′_v have Gaussian, resp. partial Gaussian, components at v | ∞, and Φ′_v partially (relative to α) transfers to Φ_v for v ∈ S. For v ∉ S, V_v is split, Φ_v = 1_{(U(V)×V)(O_{F0,v})} for a self-dual lattice, and Φ′_v = 1_{(S_n×V′_n)(O_{F0,v})}. Assume that Conjecture 2.3(a) for S_n holds over F0,v for every non-archimedean v ∉ S. Then E(h) := J(h,Φ′) − J(h,Φ) = 0 for all h ∈ H(A0). Corollary 13.5 (a separate item): under the same assumption, for every ξ ∈ F0^×, Σ_{(γ,u′)∈[(S_n(α)×V′_ξ)(F0)]} Orb((γ,u′),Φ′) = Σ_{(δ,u)∈[(U(V)(α)×V_ξ)(F0)]} Orb((δ,u),Φ).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The item bundles Theorem 13.4 (p. 955) and Corollary 13.5 (p. 956), which are separate numbered results; split them (protocol §2). 'At every place outside S' should read 'over F0,v for every non-archimedean v ∉ S' (split places are trivial). The standing hypotheses of §13.2 (p. 954) belong in the statement. The item also depends on two new issues: the proof applies Proposition 2.7(ii) in dimension n at v ∈ B, where q_v ≥ n+1 is not assumed; and the global η̃ must be unramified outside S. Review note: Missing; route 9. At v ∈ B the proof uses Proposition 2.7(ii) (item 13) in dimension n, where the printed hypothesis is q_v ≥ n+1. §13.2 puts no residue-field bound on S, so item 13 should be stated without the bound; its proof does not use it (new issue). The proof also uses two statements that no item covers: the invariance of the standard functions under K_v of the form (13.3), and the product formula for the global transfer factor (new coverage items).
items.proofOutline: For B the nonmaximal-order places, coefficients with ξ a unit at B vanish by norm-unit rank reduction; outside S∪B use maximal-order FL, and at S partial transfer. Apply Lemma13.6. Verify the q≥n hypothesis at every application of Proposition2.7.

items.name: Unit-index Fourier vanishing criterion
items.statement: Let B be a finite set of non-archimedean places of F0. Let φ be a continuous function on H(A0) = SL2(A0), left invariant under H(F0) and right invariant under a compact open K = ∏_{v∤∞} K_v ⊂ H(A_{0,f}), where K_v = m(ϖ_v^{c_v})^{-1} H(O_{F0,v}) m(ϖ_v^{c_v}) with m(ϖ^c) = diag(ϖ^c, 1) for every v ∈ B, and c_v is the largest integer with ψ_v trivial on ϖ_v^{-c_v}O_{F0,v}. Suppose W_{φ,ξ}(h∞) = 0 for all h∞ ∈ H(F0,∞) and all ξ ∈ F0^× with v(ξ) = 0 for every v ∈ B. Then φ is constant. In particular φ = 0 if φ has parallel weight n ≠ 0.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Imprecise hypothesis. The vanishing assumed is W_{φ,ξ}(h∞) = 0 identically as a function of h∞ ∈ H(F0,∞), the archimedean component only, for all ξ ∈ F0^× with v(ξ) = 0 at every v ∈ B. φ is continuous on H(A0) and left H(F0)-invariant. K_v = m(ϖ^{c_v})^{-1} SL2(O_v) m(ϖ^{c_v}) with m(ϖ^c) = diag(ϖ^c, 1), where c_v is the level of ψ_v. The weight clause is 'parallel weight n ≠ 0'. Review note: Missing; route 3 (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups, AF stages). I checked the proof on pp. 956–957. The induction step is correct: the claim for φ̃ uses K_{v0}-invariance and ψ_{v0}(ξb) = 1 when v0(ξ) ≥ 1, and the conclusion uses the fact that N(ϖ^{-c-1}O) and N^-(ϖ^cO) generate SL2. The base case needs only Fourier uniqueness for continuous functions, not absolute convergence (E2). Two inputs are not items yet: strong approximation for SL2 (planned AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.4) and the local generation lemma [27, Prop. 8.1.2]; see coverage.
items.proofOutline: Induct on B using a one-step larger unipotent translation, character orthogonality, generation of local SL2 by opposite root groups and strong approximation. Use Fourier uniqueness for continuous functions, not an unjustified absolutely convergent expansion.

items.name: Isolation of one rational invariant
items.statement: Let B = B_n be the categorical quotient (2.10) over F0. Fix b0 ∈ B(F0) and a non-archimedean place v1 of F0 that splits in F. For every place v ≠ v1 of F0, archimedean ones included, fix a compact subset Ω_v ⊂ B(F0,v) containing b0, with Ω_v = B(O_{F0,v}) for all but finitely many non-archimedean v. Then there is a neighbourhood Ω_{v1} ⊂ B(F0,v1) of b0 such that B(F0) ∩ ∏_v Ω_v = {b0} in B(A0).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Wrong hypothesis. For v ≠ v1 (archimedean places included), the Ω_v are arbitrary compact subsets of B(F0,v) containing b0. They need not be neighbourhoods of b0. In Proposition 13.8 the archimedean Ω_v is the image of (U(V)(α)×V_ξ)(F0,v), which lies in the fibre of fixed (α,ξ) and is not a neighbourhood of b0. The item as written therefore does not cover its only use. Review note: Missing; route 9. I checked the proof (a closed embedding into affine space, then the product formula applied to coordinates of y − b0). The proof does not use that v1 is split.
items.proofOutline: Embed B in affine space, bound all other coordinates and apply the number-field product formula to the difference from b0.

items.name: Individual coherent orbital equality
items.statement: Under Theorem13.4's hypotheses, matching rational regular pairs of irreducible characteristic α and nonzero norm have equal global orbital integrals.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Missing; route 9. I checked the proof on p. 958. The split place v1 enters S, with elementary matching there (Remark 13.2; new coverage item). The trivial cases where b0 ∉ Ω_v are left implicit. The misprint 'point-wise positivity of Φ_{v1}' (for Φ̃_{v1}) is recorded as a new issue.
items.proofOutline: Use Lemma13.7 and a nonnegative auxiliary split-place matching function to isolate the invariant, then cancel its nonzero local integral.

items.name: Local-to-global approximation for FL/AFL
items.statement: Let F0,v0 be a p-adic field with p odd and F_{w0}/F0,v0 unramified quadratic. Let V_{v0} be an n-dimensional F_{w0}/F0,v0-Hermitian space (split for FL, non-split for AFL). Let (g_{v0},u_{v0}) ∈ (U(V_{v0})×V_{v0})(F0,v0)_srs have integral characteristic polynomial, det(1−g_{v0}) ∈ O_{F_{w0}}^× and ⟨u_{v0},u_{v0}⟩ ≠ 0. Then the following exist. (1) A totally real field F0 whose completion at a place v0 is F0,v0 (F0 = Q when F0,v0 = Qp). (2) A totally negative ε ∈ F0^× with F := F0(√ε) and F ⊗ F0,v0 ≅ F_{w0}. (3) A totally real extension F′0/F0 of degree n, with CM field F′ = F′0(√ε). (4) An element g = c(√ε x♮) = −(1−x)/(1+x) ∈ F′^1, where x♮ ∈ F′0 and x = √ε x♮, such that O_{F_{w0}}[g] = O_{F_{w0}}[g_{v0}] in F′ ⊗_F F_{w0}. (5) A totally positive definite one-dimensional F′/F′0-Hermitian space W such that V := Res_{F′/F}W is isometric to V_{v0} at v0. (6) A vector u ∈ V such that (g,u) ∈ (U(V)×V)(F0)_srs is v0-adically as close to (g_{v0},u_{v0}) as desired. In particular the v0-adic orbital integrals of (g,u) and of its match (resp. its intersection number) equal those of the local data.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: 'Preserving the integral étale order' is inaccurate: O_{F_{w0}}[g_{v0}] need not be étale or maximal. What the construction preserves is the order itself, O_{F_{w0}}[g] = O_{F_{w0}}[g_{v0}] inside F′ ⊗_F F_{w0} (p. 959). The data should also be named: ε, F′0, the Cayley element, W, and the closeness conditions (13.5)–(13.6). Review note: Missing; route 9 (shared with the AFL branch). Its unit test is correct: in the AFL case V(v0) is non-split at v0, and the Shimura space must be split there (E23, confirmed).
api: Prove field-algebra stability under close separable coefficients, positivity at infinity and simultaneous local Hermitian conditions.
Track a split versus nonsplit local target separately.
unitTests: AFL globalizes the nonsplit special-Hom space; the Shimura nearby space must then be split at the distinguished good finite place.

items.name: Final FL induction and density extension
items.statement: The group and semi-Lie FL conclusions hold for q≥n in the unramified odd setting; extension from strongly regular nonzero-norm data to all relative regular orbits uses orbital-integral local constancy.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Missing; route 9. The statement matches Theorem 13.9 (p. 959). Two proof points: (1) the choice of S on p. 960 omits the places of residue characteristic 2, which §13.2 requires (new issue); (2) the proof establishes the identities only for the split space. The vanishing half of Conjecture 2.3 (orbital integrals of 1 at orbits matching the non-split space) is not addressed and has to be supplied by the standard functional-equation argument (sign −1 at s = 0).
items.proofOutline: Induct on rank, globalize, choose S containing all q<n and bad-order places, use nonvanishing transfers to cancel away factors, remove the Cayley determinant restriction by central scalars, then apply density. This is the proof dependency item for endpoints9–10, not a second owner.

items.name: Split derivative terms vanish
items.statement: In the incoherent test-function setup of §14, a split finite place v has ∂Jv(h,Φ′)=0.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Missing; route 9. For the rs terms the proof is the incoherence argument of Remark 14.1 (new coverage item): at a split v the away-from-v orbital integral vanishes, because no global Hermitian space realises the local data.
items.proofOutline: Use the elementary split matching and the incoherent orbit obstruction, as in Zhang[46] Proposition3.6; justify singular as well as regular terms.

items.name: Archimedean derivative detects one negative embedding
items.statement: Let v | ∞ and F′_{0,v} = F′0 ⊗_{F0} F0,v ≅ ∏_{v′|v} R. Let ξ′ ∈ F′_{0,v} be invertible, u′ ∈ V′(F0,v) with q′(u′) = ξ′, and ξ = tr_{F′_{0,v}/F0,v} ξ′. Let Φ′_v be the corrected partial Gaussian (Mihatsch–Zhang (7.6) on each rank-one factor). For h = n(b)m(a^{1/2})κ_θ, let W_ξ(h) be the product over v′ | v of the rank-one factors χ1(κ_θ)a^{1/2}e^{2πiξ′_{v′}(b+ia)}, i.e. the weight-n Whittaker factor with index ξ. (a) Orb((γ,u′),ω(h)Φ′_v) = W_ξ(h) if ξ′ is totally positive, and 0 otherwise. (b) If ξ′ is not totally positive, then ∂Orb((γ,u′),ω(h)Φ′_v) = 0 unless ξ′ is negative at exactly one v′ | v; in that case ∂Orb((γ,u′),ω(h)Φ′_v) = ½ W_ξ(h) Ei(−4πa|ξ′|_{v′}). At h = 1 the values are e^{−2π tr ξ′} and ½ e^{−2π tr ξ′} Ei(−4π|ξ′|_{v′}), where the paper prints e^{−π tr ξ′} and Ei(−2π|ξ′|_{v′}).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The item states only when the value is nonzero. Lemma 14.3 (p. 962) gives the values, and the corrected values should be stated explicitly. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The corrected formulas are Mihatsch–Zhang Proposition 7.4 ((7.7), p. 48; its footnote 5 says this paper's §12 Gaussians should be corrected), applied factor by factor over F′_{0,v}. The printed formulas belong to the uncorrected Gaussian (E12/E15). The argument is correct: the first derivative of a product with two factors vanishing at s = 0 is zero. Missing; route 9.
items.proofOutline: Factor into rank-one integrals: at least two negative components give two vanishing factors, annihilating the first derivative.

items.name: Archimedean arithmetic/analytic comparison obligation
items.statement: Let v | ∞ and ξ ∈ F0^×. Put all Gaussians, Weil actions and Kudla Green functions in the corrected convention (Mihatsch–Zhang Definition 6.6 with footnote 4, and Proposition 7.4 with footnote 5), and let ∂J_v(ξ,Φ′) be the coefficient normalized by the archimedean weight-n Whittaker function (Mihatsch–Zhang (8.20)). Then Int^K_v(ξ,Φ) = −2∂J_v(ξ,Φ′). Here ∂J_v(ξ,Φ′) = ½ Σ_{(γ,u′)} Ei(−4π|ξ′|_{v′})·Orb((γ,u′),Φ′_f) and Int^K_v(ξ,Φ) = −Σ_{(δ,u)} Ei(−4π|ξ′|_{v′})·Orb((δ,u),Φ). Both sums run over rational orbits in the ξ-fibre whose refined invariant ξ′ ∈ F′0 is negative at exactly one archimedean v′ | v. The two sets of orbits correspond bijectively, and Φ′_f and Φ are partial transfers of each other. At general h, keep a_v, i.e. Ei(−4πa_v|ξ′|_{v′}) (cf. E27).
items.locator: §14.1, Lemma 14.4, pp. 962–963, with Corollary 10.3, pp. 931–932. Corrected normalization: Mihatsch–Zhang, JEMS DOI 10.4171/JEMS/1375, Definition 6.6 and footnote 4 (p. 37), Proposition 7.4 and footnote 5 (p. 48), §8.5 (8.20)–(8.22) (pp. 56–57).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: This is an obligation, not a theorem statement, and its target identity should be stated exactly. The locator 'later §8.5' is ambiguous: it means Mihatsch–Zhang §8.5 ((8.20)–(8.22), the Whittaker normalization), not a section of this paper. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound as an obligation. Lemma 14.4 as printed is derived from the uncorrected Lemma 14.3 and Corollary 10.3 (E12, E15, E27). Mihatsch–Zhang change both the analytic Ei argument and the Green function to Ei(−4πa|·|), so the identity with factor −2 should survive, but it must be re-derived (gate G1). The proof display prints Orb((γ,u′),Φ′) where the finite part Orb((γ,u′),Φ′_f) is meant (new misprint). Missing; route 11.
items.proofOutline: Match refined orbits and use the rank-one Green integral. This item is a precise normalization-repair obligation, not a claim that unchanged printed definitions already satisfy the equality.

items.name: Holomorphic corrected derivative
items.statement: For F0=Q and compatible corrected conventions, ∂Jhol=2∂J+IntK−B is holomorphic of weight n and common Weil level.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The statement is Proposition 14.5 (p. 963) verbatim, up to the corrected conventions. Proof caveats: the log|a| cancellation rests on Jacquet [19, (10.4)], which the paper says 'verbatim applies' to the incoherent setting (not checked here). 'Independent of α' should read 'independent of a' (E21, confirmed). Missing; route 11.
items.proofOutline: Use Aexp for both terms and Weil-transfer compatibility for all cusps. Cancel nonconstant nonholomorphic terms by the archimedean comparison and the remaining log a term using Jacquet[19](10.4)'s nilpotent/coherent comparison, whose incoherent adaptation must be proved.

items.name: Conditional global arithmetic comparison
items.statement: With F0=Q and §14.3's S and standard good-place data, assume strongly regular group AFL for Sn over Qp at every p∉S. Then E♭=∂Jhol♭+Int vanishes in the fixed-level holomorphic space over R_S⊗Q Qbar.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. (cc-442dc5) Case (i) of the proof relies on item 23 beyond its printed bound; see E28 for the repair. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The proof uses exactly E♭ = ∂J♭_hol + Int (E20 confirmed; the author's AFL2019.pdf has this formula). Case (i) of the proof applies Proposition 3.9 (item 23) in Hermitian dimension n, beyond its printed bound (p_v > n+1), at p_v ∈ {n, n+1} (E28 confirmed). E28's repair (put those inert places into B) is sound. Case (ii) then uses Proposition 4.12(ii) (item 34) in dimension n, whose printed hypothesis is q ≥ n+1. The paper already does this at q_v = n, and it is harmless because the proof of part (ii) does not use the bound (new issue). Also needs η̃ unramified outside S (new issue). Missing; route 11.
items.proofOutline: Apply the unit-index Fourier criterion, using norm-unit AFL at nonmaximal-order places and maximal-order AFL elsewhere. Use the author-preprint definition without the extra printed factor2; close the Proposition3.9 bound gate.

items.name: Individual local arithmetic comparison
items.statement: Under Theorem14.6's assumptions, for every finite v∉S and ξ≠0, −2∂Jv(ξ,Φ′)=Intv(ξ,Φ) as an equality in Q log pv.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Missing; route 11. I checked the proof (p. 967): the v-terms vanish outside B, they lie in Q log p_v, and {log p_v : v ∈ B} is Q-linearly independent in R_{S,Q̄} because B ∩ S = ∅ and F0 = Q. For ξ < 0 both sides are 0.
items.proofOutline: Take Fourier coefficients of E=0; each local term lies in Q log p, finitely many are nonzero, and distinct prime logarithms remain Q-linearly independent modulo the removed-prime span. This separation uses F0=Q.

items.name: Orbitwise AFL from the global comparison
items.statement: Under the same induction assumption, at inert v∉S and for matching rational strongly regular pairs with nonzero norm, −∂Orb((γ,u′),1integral)=Intv(δ,u)log qv.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Missing; route 11. The proof display omits log q_v (E22, confirmed) and cites 'part (ii) of Theorem 14.6' where part (b) is meant (new misprint). The refinement re-applies Theorem 14.6 with S enlarged by the split place v1 of Proposition 13.8's argument.
items.proofOutline: Use invariant isolation and Theorem5.5's compact support modulo conjugation; choose nonzero away factors and cancel them. Restore log qv in the proof display.

items.name: Final AFL induction obligation
items.statement: Theorem15.1's group and semi-Lie endpoints21–22 follow by rank induction, CM globalization, the corrected global comparison and joint local constancy on the strongly regular locus. No extension to arbitrary p-adic base fields or all relative regular elements is inferred.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Both corrections it names are real. The nearby Shimura space must be split at v0: E23 confirmed, since D0 in §6.2.2 (p. 903) contains every inert v with V_v non-split, so v0 ∤ 𝔡 forces V to be split at v0. The maximal-order input must be checked at p_v ∈ {n, n+1} (E28). The local data in the proof also contain notation slips (new misprint). Missing; route 11.
items.proofOutline: Correct the nearby Shimura space to split at v0 so v0∤d is possible. Verify maximal-order input bounds and propagate every Gaussian/Green normalization correction before marking this proof closed.

items.name: Weil action preserves smooth transfer
items.statement: Theorem A.1. Let F/F0 be a quadratic extension of local fields (archimedean allowed) and V an n-dimensional F/F0-Hermitian space. If Φ′ ∈ S(S_n × V′_n) matches Φ ∈ S(U(V) × V), i.e. Definition 2.2 holds on the orbits matching V, then ω(h)Φ′ matches ω(h)Φ for every h ∈ SL2(F0). The Weil representations act on the vector variable: V′_n with ⟨u′,u′⟩ = 2u2(u1), and V with tr_{F/F0}⟨,⟩_F. Supplement, used in Proposition 14.5: the same holds for partial transfers relative to a fixed α.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The partial-transfer clause is not part of Theorem A.1 (p. 970), which is stated for full matching on a single Hermitian space V. The paper uses the partial version without proof in the proof of Proposition 14.5 (p. 963). Theorem A.1 also covers archimedean F/F0, via [43]. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound, with a proof obligation. The supplement is true: n(b) and m(a) act pointwise and preserve α-fibres and matching; w acts by a Fourier transform in the vector variable alone, so after the rank-one reduction of §12.6 (item 107) it reduces to the case n = 1 (footnote 9 argues this way for the existence of partial transfers). It is not a formal consequence of Theorem A.1 as stated. 'h ∈ H(F)' should read H(F0) (E24, confirmed). Missing; route 9.
items.proofOutline: Check upper unipotents by q equality, Levi by χV=η^n and transfer-factor scaling, and Fourier by Zhang[47]/Xue[43], including the Hermitian discriminant sign explicitly corrected in footnote10.

items.name: Hermitian Weil constants
items.statement: For an n-dimensional Hermitian space regarded as a 2n-dimensional quadratic space, χV(a)=η(a)^n and γV=η(detHerm V)ε(η,½,ψ)^n. The split vector/covector quadratic space has χ=γ=1.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Planned MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.2 is right: MP.2 covers the Weil index with its orthogonal-sum, scaling and discriminant identities. The Hermitian specialization needs λ_{F/F0}(ψ) = ε(η,½,ψ) ([20, Lemma 1.2]) and the quadratic form q(u) = ½tr_{F/F0}⟨u,u⟩, under which the rank-one check has no η(2) factor. I verified (A.1) in rank one: the discriminant is ≡ −ε, so χ_V(a) = (a,ε) = η(a).
items.proofOutline: Use orthogonal-sum multiplicativity, reduce to Hermitian rank one, and check both norm classes; retain the discriminant sign missing in the cited earlier Fourier theorem.

items.name: Formal support of a coherent sheaf
items.statement: For a noetherian formal scheme X and closed formal Y defined by J, a coherent sheaf is formally supported on Y if annihilated by some J^m. Affinely, for I-complete A and Y defined by J, this is algebraic support of its finite A-module in Spec(A/J), not only the topological support in Spf A.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Missing; route 10 (FormalSupportedIntersections). Matches p. 971.
api: Construct supported coherent categories, change of ideal and finite-thickening equivalence.
unitTests: On Spf A the topological support can be too coarse to detect J-power torsion.

items.name: Coherent and supported perfect Grothendieck groups
items.statement: Let X be a noetherian formal scheme and Y ⊂ X a closed formal subscheme. K′_0(X) (= G0(X)) is the Grothendieck group of the abelian category of coherent O_X-modules. K_0^Y(X) is the abelian group generated by the classes of bounded complexes of locally free coherent O_X-modules whose homology sheaves are formally supported on Y, subject to [E·] = [E′·] + [E″·] for short exact sequences of such complexes and [E·] = [F·] whenever E· and F· are quasi-isomorphic (Gillet–Soulé [11, §1.2]). K_0(X) := K_0^X(X). TauCeti.ExactK0 presents K′_0 directly; K_0^Y needs the quasi-isomorphism relations in addition.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: K_0^Y(X) is not the plain exact-category K0 of the category of complexes. Gillet–Soulé's K_0^Y ([11, §1.2], cited on p. 972) also identifies quasi-isomorphic complexes, so acyclic complexes have class 0. 'Use the existing exact-category Grothendieck group as the algebraic presentation' is right for K′_0 = G0 (coherent sheaves) only. Review note: Missing; route 10.
api: Construct relations, class maps, exact functoriality, cup product and support change; distinguish globally strictly perfect from locally perfect unless a resolution property is proved.
unitTests: The Cartan equivalence is not definitional on singular X.

items.name: Dimension and codimension filtrations
items.statement: Let X be a noetherian formal scheme and Y ⊂ X closed. Define F^iK_0^Y(X) := ∪_{Z⊂Y closed, codim_X Z ≥ i} Im(K_0^Z(X) → K_0^Y(X)). This is a directed union of subgroups, hence a subgroup, and gives a descending filtration with Gr^iK_0^Y(X) := F^iK_0^Y(X)/F^{i+1}K_0^Y(X) ((B.1)–(B.2)). Define F_iK′_0(X) := ∪_{Z⊂X closed, dim Z ≤ i} Im(K′_0(Z) → K′_0(X)), an ascending filtration. Where needed, rational versions are obtained by tensoring with Q.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: 'With rational coefficients throughout the paper' is not what the paper says. (B.1)–(B.2) and F_iK′_0 are defined integrally (p. 972). Rational coefficients enter with the Adams decomposition and (B.3), and in multiplicities such as mult_C ∈ Q (proof of Proposition 5.2). Review note: Missing; route 10.
api: Construct monotonicity, boundedness and finite-pushforward compatibility; interpret unions through directed finite unions of supports.
unitTests: Codimension filtration is decreasing; dimension filtration is increasing.

items.name: Regular supported K/G comparison
items.statement: For regular pure-dimensional finite-dimensional X in a category with the required resolution/devissage theorem, K0^Y(X)≅G0(Y) and F^(d−i) corresponds to Fi. The formal-scheme extension requires verification, not an automatic consequence of scheme devissage.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Missing; route 10. The paper asserts this for regular noetherian formal schemes of pure dimension d without proof ('the definitions in [11, §1] carry over'), and the item rightly treats the formal case as a closure gate.
items.proofOutline: Construct the coherent-to-perfect resolutions and supported devissage; verify global resolution assumptions or use local perfect complexes. The arbitrary formal statement is a closure gate.

items.name: Scheme rational Adams decomposition
items.statement: For the regular schemes in Gillet–Soulé's hypotheses, supported rational K0 decomposes into Adams weight spaces, and the codimension filtration is the sum of weights at least its index.
items.locator: Appendix B.1, p. 972, citing [11, Prop. 5.3] (and [11, Prop. 5.5] for (B.3))
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Statement matches p. 972 (X a regular scheme of pure dimension d; K^Y_0(X)_Q = ⊕_i K^Y_0(X)^{(i)}_Q with ψ^k = k^i, and F^j = ⊕_{i≥j}). SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.4 (codimension filtration) and S.6 (Adams operations, rational projectors) plan it; status planned is right.
items.proofOutline: Import Adams operations and prove the rational projectors in the finite weight range; identify the support filtration with the source's one.

items.name: Scheme support-filtration multiplication
items.statement: Under the scheme hypotheses of Gillet–Soulé[11] Proposition5.5, F^j1K0^Y(X)Q · F^j2K0^Z(X)Q ⊂ F^(j1+j2)K0^(Y∩Z)(X)Q.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Planned SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.6 is plausible (products with supports, Adams operations). The identification of the codimension filtration with Adams weights that it relies on (item 132, GS Prop. 5.3) is closer to S.7's γ-filtration comparison. Note for the §7 reviewer, not checked here: the scheme case of (B.3) is applied in (7.15) to Hk[K g K] over the moduli stack M, which is beyond [11]'s scheme setting.
items.proofOutline: Use Adams weights and cup-product compatibility. The paper explicitly only expects the analogous formal assertion; it is not extracted as proved.

items.name: Locally noetherian formal K-groups
items.statement: For an increasing directed cover by noetherian formal opens Xi, define the paper's K0, G0 and supported K0 as inverse limits along restrictions, together with their filtrations. Verify independence of the exhaustion and identify the comparison with a global categorical construction where available.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Missing; route 10. Matches p. 973. Independence of the exhaustion follows by cofinality, because a noetherian open is quasi-compact and so lies in a single X_i when the union is directed.
api: Construct restriction systems and canonical comparison maps; do not confuse this open-exhaustion limit with continuous K-theory of nilpotent thickenings.
unitTests: A one-open exhaustion returns the noetherian group.

items.name: Proper torsion Euler degree
items.statement: For W a scheme proper over Spf A, A a complete DVR, define degree([E])=Σi(−1)^i lengthA Riπ*E; the scheme-over-Spf and properness assumptions force finite-length cohomology. For derived intersections sum (−1)^(i+j)length Riπ*Torj.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Missing; route 10. Matches (B.4)–(B.5), p. 973. Finite length holds because a scheme proper over Spf A is killed by a fixed power of the uniformizer, and so are the thickenings of Y ∩ Z that carry the Tor sheaves.
api: Construct additive Euler degree, supported derived pairing and base-change length formula.
unitTests: A general proper formal scheme can have nontorsion cohomology and is not covered by this degree map.

items.name: Closed-union G0 decomposition modulo overlap
items.statement: Let X be a noetherian formal scheme and X = X1 ∪ X2 with closed formal subschemes X_i = V(I_i), I_1 ∩ I_2 = 0. Then [E] ↦ ([E⊗O_{X1}], [E⊗O_{X2}]) induces an isomorphism coker(K′_0(X1∩X2) → K′_0(X)) ≅ coker(K′_0(X1∩X2) → K′_0(X1)) ⊕ coker(K′_0(X1∩X2) → K′_0(X2)), whose inverse is induced by (a1,a2) ↦ i_{1*}a1 + i_{2*}a2. For locally noetherian X with the inverse-limit groups of B.1, use the inverse limits of these cokernels, or prove the Mittag-Leffler property needed to commute cokernels with the limit.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: The item omits the setting. The paper states the lemma for locally noetherian formal schemes of the type in B.1 (inverse-limit K-groups), but its proof treats only noetherian X, after an unjustified 'immediate' reduction (new issue). The map [E] ↦ ([E⊗O_{X1}], [E⊗O_{X2}]) is well defined only modulo the images of K′_0(X1∩X2), since the Tor_1 error terms are supported on X1∩X2; the item's proofOutline already notes this. Review note: Missing; route 10. I checked the proof for noetherian X: the four-term Tor sequence gives one composite, and the other is immediate because E⊗O_{X2} is an O_{X1∩X2}-module when E is an O_{X1}-module.
items.proofOutline: Tensor the closed-union exact sequence; the Tor error and intersection quotient are supported on the overlap. Prove the displayed ordinary restriction formula descends to these cokernels.

items.name: Expected-dimensional Tor vanishing
items.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian formal scheme of pure finite dimension, and let Z1, Z2 ⊂ X be pure-dimensional closed formal subschemes such that Z1 → X is a regular immersion and Z2 is Cohen–Macaulay. If codim_X(Z1∩Z2) = codim_X Z1 + codim_X Z2 at every point of Z1∩Z2, then Tor_i^{O_X}(O_{Z1},O_{Z2}) = 0 for all i > 0. In particular O_{Z1} ⊗^L O_{Z2} = O_{Z1} ⊗ O_{Z2} = O_{Z1∩Z2} in K′_0(Z1∩Z2).
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Wording. 'Z1→X regular' should read 'the closed immersion Z1 → X is a regular immersion' (for example, when X and Z1 are both regular). 'Expected codimension' means codim_X(Z1∩Z2) = codim_X Z1 + codim_X Z2 at every point of Z1∩Z2. Review note: Missing; route 10. I checked the proof: the Koszul complex of a local regular sequence, whose image is a regular sequence in the CM ring O_{Z2,x} by the dimension count, with codim read locally as dim O_{X,x} − dim O_{Z,x}. The paper uses the lemma only in the proof of Lemma 4.4 (p. 889).
items.proofOutline: Resolve Z1 by the Koszul complex of its local regular sequence. Expected height and Cohen–Macaulayness make the restricted sequence regular on Z2; prove the localization/gluing steps and dimension hypotheses.

items.name: Tor vanishing on an expected component
items.statement: Under LemmaB.2's ambient hypotheses, if Z1∩Z2=Y∪Y′ with Y of expected dimension, higher Tor restricted to Y vanishes in G0(Y) modulo the image from Y∩Y′.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Missing; route 10. It follows because near points of Y \ Y′ the intersection equals Y, so the restricted Tor sheaves are supported on Y∩Y′ and their classes lie in the image of K′_0(Y∩Y′) (dévissage). The paper does not use this part elsewhere.
items.proofOutline: Apply local expected-dimensional Tor vanishing away from the overlap and LemmaB.1's cokernel comparison. Do not claim the sheaf itself vanishes on the overlap.

items.name: Supported K-to-Chow comparison
items.statement: For the regular arithmetic schemes used in §9, the rational dimension-one associated graded of coherent K-theory with prescribed support identifies with the corresponding supported Chow group, compatibly with finite proper pushforward.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Status planned SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.7: acceptable. S.7 plans 'the γ-filtration and the comparison with Chow groups in the regular setting'. The paper needs the version with supports: for M regular and Y the image of CM(α,g), Gr_1K′_{0,Y}(M)_Q ≅ Ch_{1,Y}(M)_Q ([11, Th. 8.2]), compatible with finite pushforward. S.7's description does not mention supports (S.6 and KU-schemek handle supports), so the design job must state the supported form in S.7.
items.proofOutline: Use the shared rational Chern-character/Riemann–Roch construction and verify its grading and support compatibility.

items.name: Chow operations for the cycle construction
items.statement: Use rational equivalence, proper pushforward with residue multiplicities, flat/lci pullback, Chern classes and projection/excess-intersection formulas on the actual schemes/stacks in the moduli problem; a finite unramified divisor map need not be a closed immersion.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Status planned SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5: partly. SF.5 plans Chow groups, proper pushforward, flat/lci pullback and Chern classes from Fulton, stated over a field. §§7–9 use them for schemes of finite type over the Dedekind base O_E[1/d] (Fulton Ch. 20), with supports (Ch_{1,CM(α,g)}(M)) and residue-degree multiplicities in proper pushforward. SF.5 must be confirmed to cover the relative case over a Dedekind base, or a link to the owner of relative Chow groups added.
api: Import the generic Chow operations once and verify each morphism's proper/flat/lci conditions.
unitTests: A finite degree-d map multiplies the pushed-forward point cycle by d.

items.name: Existing abstract exact Grothendieck group
items.statement: TauCeti.ExactK0 E is the free abelian group on object isomorphism classes in an essentially small additive category with exact structure E, modulo conflation relations. It is a reusable carrier, not formal-scheme G0 by itself.
items.locator: Appendix B foundational input; TauCeti/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup/Exact.lean:162 (def TauCeti.ExactK0) at f790474.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Library claim verified at f790474: ExactK0 E := PresentedK0 (exactRelations E), the free abelian group on object classes modulo [X₂] = [X₁] + [X₃] for every E-conflation. It requires C essentially small and preadditive, with a zero object and binary biproducts. It serves as the carrier for K′_0 only; K_0^Y also needs quasi-isomorphism relations (item 129).
api: Reuse the class map and conflation-additive universal property after constructing the appropriate exact category.
unitTests: A split conflation gives [X⊕Y]=[X]+[Y].

items.name: Existing regular-sequence carrier
items.statement: Mathlib's RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular M rs requires successive scalar multiplication to be regular on the preceding quotient and the final quotient to be nonzero. It supplies the algebraic predicate, not the Koszul resolution or formal Tor theorem.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Library claim verified at 082e2d3 in Mathlib/RingTheory/Regular/RegularSequence.lean. Line 135 is RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular: rs[i] is SMul-regular on M/(rs.take i)M. Line 146 is IsRegular, which extends it with ⊤ ≠ Ideal.ofList rs • ⊤. The item statement is accurate.
api: Reuse IsWeaklyRegular and IsRegular; prove the source's commutative-algebra consequences separately.
unitTests: Distinguish weak regularity from the final nonzero-quotient condition.

items.name: Existing real Gaussian Fourier formula
items.statement: For complex b with positive real part, the real Fourier transform of exp(−πbx²) is b^(−1/2)exp(−πt²/b), in Mathlib's real Fourier convention.
items.locator: Supplement (Mathlib input, not a statement of the paper); used for §12's Gaussian Fourier transforms
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Checked at Mathlib 082e2d3: fourier_gaussian_pi (Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gaussian/FourierTransform.lean:227) states 𝓕(x ↦ cexp(−π b x²)) = (t ↦ 1/b^{1/2}·cexp(−π/b·t²)) for 0 < re b. This matches the item. Mathlib's transform uses e^{−2πixt} and the paper's uses ψ(+⟨x,y⟩); for even Gaussians the two agree.
items.proofOutline: Reuse the pinned theorem and prove the sign/measure/scalar-restriction adapter needed for the paper's Hermitian Fourier transform.

items.name: Existing real-line Poisson formula
items.statement: For a complex-valued Schwartz function f on R, Σn∈Z f(x+n)=Σn∈Z Fourier(f)(n)e(nx). This is not the adelic Poisson theorem used in §12.
items.locator: Supplement (Mathlib input, not a statement of the paper)
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Checked at Mathlib 082e2d3: SchwartzMap.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier (Analysis/Fourier/PoissonSummation.lean:219) states Σ_{n∈Z} f(x+n) = Σ_{n∈Z} 𝓕f(n)·fourier n (x : UnitAddCircle) for f ∈ 𝓢(ℝ,ℂ). This matches the item. The adelic version used in the proof of Theorem 12.9 is planned in AL.0.
items.proofOutline: Reuse the real theorem as an archimedean test only; construct the adelic theorem in AL.0.

items.name: Existing dominated parameter differentiation
items.statement: Under neighbourhood-wise a.e. differentiability, measurability and an integrable bound on the derivatives, differentiation commutes with the integral at the specified parameter, and the derivative integrand is integrable.
items.locator: Supplement (Mathlib input, not a statement of the paper)
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Checked at Mathlib 082e2d3: hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le (Analysis/Calculus/ParametricIntegral.lean:288). It is stated for parameters in any RCLike 𝕜, so complex s is covered, and it also needs F x₀ integrable. It matches the item.
items.proofOutline: Apply the pinned generic theorem only after proving the local orbital/height domination hypotheses.

items.name: Existing Schur determinant identity
items.statement: For square blocks over a commutative ring, with the bottom-right block D invertible, det([A B;C D])=det(D)det(A−BD⁻¹C).
items.locator: §4.1, proof of Lemma 4.1 (third equality of (4.5)), p. 886; Mathlib Matrix.det_fromBlocks₂₂
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Checked at Mathlib 082e2d3, Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/SchurComplement.lean:384: theorem det_fromBlocks₂₂ (A : Matrix m m α) (B : Matrix m n α) (C : Matrix n m α) (D : Matrix n n α) [Invertible D] : (fromBlocks A B C D).det = det D * det (A − B * ⅟D * C), over a commutative ring α. The item states it correctly (A and D square, B and C rectangular); status library is right. It is the extraction's own supplement, not a result of the paper, and it is sound.
items.proofOutline: Reuse Matrix.det_fromBlocks₂₂ for the determinant step; prove the Hermitian/unitary and domain adapters separately.

items.name: Existing Cayley–Hamilton theorem
items.statement: A square matrix over a commutative ring annihilates its characteristic polynomial.
items.note: Statement uses the conventions and standing hypotheses explicitly recorded in the report. No formalization is claimed. Review note: Status library: verified. mathlib:Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Charpoly/Basic.lean:216 at 082e2d3) states aeval M M.charpoly = 0 for M : Matrix n n R, R commutative. Lemma 7.15 applies it to an F⊗Q_ℓ-linear endomorphism of the free module V_ℓ(A), so also cite mathlib:LinearMap.aeval_self_charpoly (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Charpoly/Basic.lean:89; Module.Free and Module.Finite over a commutative ring). The converse direction of Lemma 7.15 (α(ϕ) = 0 with α irreducible of degree n ⇒ char_F(ϕ) = α) is not Cayley–Hamilton. It needs that the characteristic and minimal polynomials have the same irreducible factors, and this belongs in item 60.
items.proofOutline: Reuse the matrix theorem after the F-linear Tate representation and its independence have been constructed.

items.name: Conjecture 3.2 (statement only)
items.statement: Let F/F0 be an unramified quadratic extension of p-adic fields with p odd, q the residue cardinality of F0, and V_n the non-split n-dimensional hermitian space of §3.1. (a) If γ ∈ S_n(F0)_rs matches g ∈ U(V_n)(F0)_rs, then ∂Orb(γ, 1_{S_n(O_{F0})}) = −Int(g)·log q, with Int(g) as in (3.8). (b) If (γ,u′) ∈ (S_n×V′_n)(F0)_rs matches (g,u) ∈ (U(V_n)×V_n)(F0)_rs, then ∂Orb((γ,u′), 1_{(S_n×V′_n)(O_{F0})}) = −Int(g,u)·log q, with Int(g,u) as in (3.13). ∂Orb includes the transfer factors (2.16)–(2.17). A conjecture; the paper proves the srs case (Conjecture 3.8) as Theorem 15.1.
items.note: Added by cc-442dc5: a numbered statement without its own item. A conjecture; no proof is claimed. Review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21): statement corrected against the paper: Minor: the item omits the standing hypotheses of §3 (F/F0 an unramified quadratic extension of p-adic fields, p odd; V_n the non-split space of §3.1; ∂Orb with the §2.3 transfer factors and η̃ = (−1)^v).
items.proofOutline: A conjecture the paper states; the proved endpoint is items 21–22.

items.name: Regular semisimple points and cyclic-vector criteria
items.statement: Let F0 be a field of characteristic 0 and H a reductive F0-group acting on an affine F0-variety X. A point x ∈ X(F0) is H-semisimple if H·x is Zariski closed in X (for F0 local, equivalently if H(F0)·x is closed in X(F0) in the analytic topology), H-regular if the stabiliser H_x is trivial, and regular semisimple (rs) if both.
