X(F0)_rs denotes the rs points, [X(F0)]_rs the rs H(F0)-orbits, and X → X//H the categorical quotient. For the actions of §2: (a) g′ ∈ U(V♯) is rs for the conjugation action of U(V), V = u0^⊥, iff (g′^i u0)_{0≤i≤n−1} is an F-basis of V♯. (b) (g,u) ∈ U(V)×V with dim V = m is rs iff (g^i u)_{0≤i≤m−1} is an F-basis of V. (c) γ ∈ S_n is rs for GL_{n−1} iff (γ^i e)_{0≤i≤n−1} is a basis of F^n and (e*γ^i)_{0≤i≤n−1} a basis of (F^n)*. (d) (γ,(u1,u2)) ∈ S_m×V′_m is rs iff (γ^i u1)_{i<m} and (u2 γ^i)_{i<m} are bases. (a) is used in the proof of Lemma 4.3; (c)–(d) are the standard criteria of [46, §2] and [29], used without proof.
items.locator: §1.2, Notation on algebra, pp. 868–869; §4.1, proof of Lemma 4.3(i), p. 887
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): No item defines 'regular semisimple' or gives the cyclic-vector criteria, although every item from 5 on uses them. The paper uses the unitary criterion in the proof of Lemma 4.3(i) and the linear one implicitly in Lemma 4.9. Suggested owner: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison (route 9, part-ii) Route: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison.

items.name: Self-dual hermitian lattices in the unramified case
items.statement: Let F/F0 be an unramified quadratic extension of p-adic fields with p odd, and V a non-degenerate F/F0-hermitian space. V contains a self-dual O_F-lattice iff v(det V) is even (V 'split'). Any two self-dual lattices are U(V)(F0)-conjugate, and the stabiliser of one is a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup. If u0 ∈ V has ⟨u0,u0⟩ ∈ O_{F0}^× and Λ0 ⊂ u0^⊥ is self-dual, then Λ♯_0 = Λ0 ⊕ O_F u0 is self-dual. In each dimension there are exactly two isometry classes, V0 (split) and V1 (non-split), and V♯_i = V_i ⊕ F u0 with ⟨u0,u0⟩ a unit is split iff V_i is. The Haar measures on GL_{n−1}(F0) and U(V0)(F0) are normalised by vol(GL_{n−1}(O_{F0})) = vol(K0) = 1, K0 = Stab(Λ0).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): The unit test functions of the FL and AFL and the measure normalisation rest on these facts, and no item states them. Items 7, 9 and 10 only mention the volumes. Owner: GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.2 (local classification of hermitian lattices); the hyperspecial and measure clauses go to JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison

items.name: Unitary orbital rank reduction for the FL
items.statement: Let F/F0 be unramified with p odd, V♯_0 = V0 ⊕ F u0 split with ⟨u0,u0⟩ = 1, Λ♯_0 = Λ0 ⊕ O_F u0 self-dual, K♯_0 = Stab(Λ♯_0) and K0 = Stab(Λ0). Let g′ ∈ U(V♯_0)(F0)_rs and ξ ∈ F^1 with 1−ξd ∈ O_F^× and det(1−ξg′) ∈ O_F^×. Then for h ∈ U(V0)(F0), h^{−1}ξg′h ∈ K♯_0 iff h·r(ξg′) ∈ K0 × Λ0 iff h·r♮(ξg′) ∈ K0 × Λ0. Hence Orb(g′, 1_{K♯_0}) = Orb(r_ξ(g′), 1_{K0×Λ0}) = Orb(r♮_ξ(g′), 1_{K0×Λ0}). Proof as for Lemma 4.11: the Cayley transform preserves integrality when det(1−g′) and det(1+x) = 2^{n−1}(1−d)/det(1−g′) are units, and (1−g) ∈ GL(Λ0) converts ũ to the block vector.
items.locator: §2.4, proof of Proposition 2.7, p. 879 (unitary counterpart of §4.3, Lemma 4.11, p. 894)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): Proposition 2.7 (FL), and so Theorem 13.9, needs the unitary analogue of Lemma 4.11. The paper never states it, and item 12 mentions it only in its outline. Suggested owner: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison (route 9, part-ii) Route: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison.

items.name: Transfer factors are preserved by the Cayley chart
items.statement: Let F/F0 be unramified with η̃ = (−1)^v. Write γ′ = (a b; c d) ∈ S_n(F0)_rs with 1−d ∈ O_F^× and det(1−γ′) ∈ O_F^×, and let r(γ′) = (γ,(u1,u2)) with u1 = b̃/√ε. Then det(γ′^i e)_{0≤i≤n−1} = det(a^i b)_{0≤i≤n−2} and det(γ^i u1)_{0≤i≤n−2} = (2/((1−d)√ε))^{n−1} det(1−γ)^{−1} det(a^i b)_{0≤i≤n−2}; det γ′ and det γ have norm 1. Hence ω(γ′) = ω(r(γ′)) = ω(r♮(γ′)), and ω(ξγ′) = ω(γ′) for ξ ∈ F^1.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): The derivative identity ∂Orb(γ′) = ∂Orb(r(γ′)) needs ω(γ′) = ω(r(γ′)). The paper imports it, and no item states it. The identity below was checked numerically (n = 5). Suggested owner: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison (route 9, part-ii) Route: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison.

items.name: Local constancy against strata cycles in all dimensions; (B.3)-free Proposition 5.2
items.statement: Let n ≥ 3 and Λ ⊂ V_n a vertex lattice of maximal type. For every i and every C ∈ Ch_{i,V(Λ)}(N_{n,red}), u ↦ χ(N_n, C ⊗^L O_{Z(u)}) on V_n∖{0} is locally constant and compactly supported, and constant near 0 ([26, §6.4]). Consequently Proposition 5.2 holds without (B.3). Write the restriction of LN^g_n to a noetherian open N°_n as Σ_C mult_C [O_C] over integral closed formal subschemes C ⊂ N^g_n of any dimension. Vertical C are handled by the statement above; horizontal C by (5.1), since Z(u) is Cartier and C ⊄ Z(u); 0-dimensional C pair to 0 with a Cartier divisor.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): Formal-scheme (B.3) is unproved (E26), and the extraction chose Remark 5.3's route for Proposition 5.2. That route needs Lemma 5.1 for cycles of every dimension ([26, §6.4]), which no item states. Item 36 has dimension 1 only. Suggested owner: UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (route 11, part-ii) Route: UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles.

items.name: Li–Zhang inputs for strata curves
items.statement: Let n ≥ 3 and Λ ⊂ V_n a vertex lattice of maximal type. Ch_1(V(Λ))_Q is spanned by the classes [V(Λ′)] of the Deligne–Lusztig curves V(Λ′) for vertex lattices Λ′ ⊃ Λ of type 3. For each type-3 vertex lattice Λ′, u ↦ χ(N_n, O_{V(Λ′)} ⊗^L O_{Z(u)}) on V_n∖{0} is locally constant and compactly supported, and constant on a punctured neighbourhood of 0.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): Lemma 5.1 rests entirely on two external facts: curve classes on V(Λ) are spanned by type-3 strata, and the type-3 local constancy of Li–Zhang. No item states either. Suggested owner: UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (route 11, part-ii) Route: UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles.

items.name: Vertex-lattice support criterion
items.statement: Let x ∈ N_n(k̄), and let V(Λ) be the smallest Bruhat–Tits stratum containing x. If x ∈ Z(u), then u ∈ Λ ([24, Prop. 4.1]). If x ∈ N^g_n, then gΛ = Λ. U(V_n)(F0) acts transitively on the vertex lattices of each type t ∈ {1, 3, …, 2⌊(n−1)/2⌋+1}. Hence the support of Int on (U(V_n)×V_n)(F0)_srs lies in U(V_n)(F0)·⋃_t (K_{Λ_t} × Λ_t), which is compact modulo U(V_n)(F0).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): Item 40's outline quotes these facts, but no item states them; they are the whole content of the compactness assertion. Suggested owner: UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (route 11, part-ii) Route: UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles.

items.name: Projection-formula form of the semi-Lie intersection number
items.statement: For (g,u) ∈ (U(V_n)×V_n)(F0)_rs, RΔ_*(LN^g_n ⊗^L_{O_{N_n}} O_{Z(u)}) = O_{Γ_g} ⊗^L_{O_{N_n×N_n}} O_{Δ(Z(u))} in K_0^{Γ_g∩Δ(Z(u))}(N_n × N_n), using RΔ_*O_{Z(u)} = O_{Δ(Z(u))} for the closed immersion Δ. Hence Int(g,u) = χ(N_n × N_n, O_{Γ_g} ⊗^L O_{Δ(Z(u))}).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): An equivalent definition of Int(g,u) on N_n × N_n. Mihatsch–Zhang (JEMS, (9.8)) take it as their definition, and it links (3.13) to Liu's Fourier–Jacobi formulation [30]. No item states it; item 19 only asks for the projection formula in its API. Suggested owner: UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (route 11, part-ii) Route: UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles.

items.name: Nearby hermitian spaces
items.statement: Let V be the n-dimensional F/F0-hermitian space of §6.1: signature (n−1,1) at the real place below ϕ0, positive definite at the other real places of F0. (a) For a finite place v0 of F0 inert in F, there is a unique F/F0-hermitian space V′ = V^{(v0)} of dimension n, up to isometry, that is positive definite at every real place, isometric to V_v at every finite v ≠ v0, and not isometric to V_{v0} at v0. (b) For a real place v0 of F0, there is a unique V′ = V^{(v0)} with signature (n−1,1) at v0, positive definite at the other real places, and V′_v ≅ V_v at every finite v. In both cases the local invariants change at exactly two places, so existence and uniqueness follow from Landherr's theorem (the Hasse principle for hermitian forms with the product formula for local determinant signs). G′ := U(V′), with fixed isomorphisms G′(A^{v0}_{0,f}) ≅ G(A^{v0}_{0,f}) (resp. G′(A_{0,f}) ≅ G(A_{0,f})).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): Both uniformizations (7.3)–(7.6) and (8.3)–(8.5), Propositions 7.4, 7.16, 7.17, 8.2 and Theorems 9.4 and 10.1 are stated with V′. Its existence and uniqueness is Landherr's local–global theorem, which no item states. Suggested owner: UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 8) Route: UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels.

items.name: RSZ generic fibre is the canonical model
items.statement: For every K_G̃ = K_{ZQ} × K_G, the generic fibre of M_{K_G̃}(G̃) (Definition 6.1), equivalently the moduli functor (6.13) over E, is isomorphic to the canonical model of Sh_{K_G̃}(G̃,{h_G̃}) over E = E_Φ E_r ([40, Prop. 3.5]). After base change along any embedding ν: E → C it is a disjoint union, indexed by ZQ(Q)\ZQ(A_f)/K_{ZQ}, of copies of Sh_{K_G}(Res_{F0/Q}U(V),{h_G}) (from (6.6)). Each copy is G′(F0)\[D_{v0} × G(A_{0,f})/K_G] as in (8.3)–(8.5), where v0 is the real place below ν|_F.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): Theorem 8.1 is proved on the canonical model and transferred to the moduli generic fibre, and (8.3) uniformizes M_{ν,C}. The comparison of the generic fibre with the canonical model is an imported theorem that no item states; items 44 and 45 mention it only in notes. Suggested owner: UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (route 8) Route: UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels.

items.name: Automorphic line bundle and its Petersson metric
items.statement: ω is the automorphic line bundle on M_{K_G̃}(G̃) of [22]: on each fibre (8.5) over C it is the descent of the tautological line bundle z ↦ z on D_{v0}, with the duality convention of [22]/[5]. c1(ω) ∈ Ch^1(M_{K_G̃}(G̃))_Q. ω̂ = (ω, ||·||_Pet) is the extension of ω to the integral model M over O_E[1/d], with the Petersson metric normalized as in [5, §7.2], and ĉ1(ω̂) ∈ Ĉh^1(M). The constant in the metric changes Int(0,Φ) and must be taken from [5, §7.2].
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): The zero coefficients Z(0,φ) = −φ(0)c1(ω), Ẑ_B(0,φ) = −φ(0)ĉ1(ω̂) and Int(0,Φ) (9.9) depend on ω, on its extension over O_E[1/d] and on the Petersson metric. No item defines them; items 66, 74 and 78 only use them. Suggested owner: UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (route 11) Route: UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles.

items.name: Kudla Green functions are Green functions for KR divisors
items.statement: For u ∈ V′(F0)∖{0} and h∞ ∈ ∏_{v|∞}SL2(F_{0,v}), GK(u,h∞) is smooth on D_{v0}∖D_{v0,u}, has a logarithmic singularity along D_{v0,u}, and dd^c GK(u,h∞) + δ_{D_{v0,u}} is a smooth (1,1)-form ([23, Prop. 11.1]; unitary case [28, §4B]). D_{v0,u} ≠ ∅ if and only if ⟨u,u⟩ ∈ F_{0,+}; otherwise GK(u,h∞) is smooth. Consequently, for ξ ∈ F0 and φ ∈ S(V(A_{0,f}))^{K_G}, the sum (8.13) is locally finite on D_{v0} × G(A_{0,f})/K_G. It descends to the fibre (8.5) as a Green function for Z(ξ,φ)⊗_{E,ν}C when ξ ∈ F_{0,+}, and to a smooth function otherwise ([28, Prop. 4.9]). The normalization must be GK = −Ei(4πa_{v0}R(u,z)), matching q^ξ (see the new issue on (8.11)).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): The paper states that (8.11) has a logarithmic singularity along D_{v0,u} and that (8.13) 'defines a Green function for the divisor Z(ξ,φ)'. The arithmetic divisor classes and the archimedean pairing depend on this, and no item states it. Suggested owner: UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (route 11) Route: UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles.

items.name: Complex uniformization of the CM cycles
items.statement: Let ν be a complex place of E over the real place v0 of F0, V′ = V^{(v0)} the archimedean nearby space, and G′ = U(V′). Let α ∈ A_n(O_{F0}[1/d]) be irreducible over F with F′ CM, and g ∈ G(F_{0,d}). Every δ ∈ G′(α)(F0) has a unique fixed point z_δ ∈ D_{v0}, its negative eigenline. On each fibre (8.5) of (8.4), the complex points of CM(α,g)⊗_{E,ν}C are the images of (z_δ, hK_G) for (δ,h) ∈ G′(F0)\(G′(α)(F0) × G(A_{0,f})/K_G) with h^{-1}δh ∈ K^d_G × K_{G,d}gK_{G,d}; G′(F0) acts freely under the smallness assumption. CM(α,g)_E is finite étale over E, and the intersection of Hk_E with the diagonal is proper and of expected dimension 0 in a smooth ambient, so LCM(α,g)_{ν,C} is the reduced 0-cycle. Hence, on each fibre, LCM(α,φ0)_{ν,C} = Σ_{(δ,h)} φ0(h^{-1}δh)·[(z_δ,hK_G)].
items.locator: §10, proof of Theorem 10.1, p. 930 (implicit; archimedean analogue of Proposition 7.17, pp. 917–918)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): Theorem 10.1 needs the archimedean analogue of Proposition 7.17: the complex points of CM(α,g) in the uniformization (8.5), and the fact that the derived class equals the naive 0-cycle on the generic fibre. The paper leaves this implicit and no item states it. Suggested owner: UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (route 11) Route: UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles.

items.name: Unitary Gaussian: orbital integral and Weil action
items.statement: Let V be a positive-definite hermitian space of dimension n over C/R, with q(u) = ⟨u,u⟩ the hermitian norm. Let G = U(V) carry the Haar measure of total mass 1, let ψ(x) = e^{2πix}, and let ω be the Weil representation (11.1) of SL2(R) on S(V), with V viewed as a 2n-dimensional real quadratic space with form q; ω acts on S((G×V)(R)) through V. Let Φ(g,u) = 1_{G(R)}(g)e^{−2πq(u)}; the paper prints e^{−π⟨u,u⟩}. Then Orb((g,u),Φ) = e^{−2πq(u)} for every regular semisimple (g,u). For h = n(b)m(a^{1/2})κθ with a > 0 and b ∈ R, ω(h)Φ(g,u) = χ_n(κθ)a^{n/2}e^{2πiq(u)(b+ia)}1_{G(R)}(g); in particular ω(κθ)Φ = χ_n(κθ)Φ. For n = 1 the function is φ(z) = e^{−2πzz̄}, and φ̂ = φ for the self-dual measure of the pairing tr(z w̄).
items.locator: §12.1, (12.1)–(12.4) and the display after (12.4), p. 940; §12.3, first display, p. 941; Gaussian corrected per Mihatsch–Zhang, JEMS (DOI 10.4171/JEMS/1375), §7.3, p. 49, footnotes 3 (p. 18) and 5 (p. 48)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): Two facts about the unitary Gaussian are used later: its orbital integral, and its SL2(R)-action of weight n. Proposition 13.3 uses them for the weight of J(h,Φ), and Lemma 14.4 and Proposition 14.5 use them too. Item 97 names the corrected Gaussian but states neither fact. Both need the Mihatsch–Zhang correction (E12) and a^{n/2} in place of the printed |a|^{1/2} (E13). Suggested owner: none; owner: the Jacquet–Rallis Part II (route 9, JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison), importing the Weil representation formulas from MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.2 Route: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison.

items.name: Norm estimates on affine G-varieties (Beuzart-Plessis, App. A.1)
items.statement: Let F0 be a number field and let a reductive group G over F0 act on an affine variety X. Let π: X → B = X//G, let Δ be a regular function on B with B_rs = {Δ ≠ 0}, and let X_rs = π^{−1}(B_rs). Suppose π_rs: X_rs → B_rs is a G-torsor. Fix norms ‖·‖_X, ‖·‖_{X_rs} and ‖·‖_{B_rs} on adelic points, as products of local norms, and on local points; on the affine line use ‖t‖_v = max(1,|t|_v). Then the following hold. (ii) For a morphism f: Y → Z of affine varieties there is d > 0 with ‖f(y)‖ ≪ ‖y‖^d, locally uniformly in v. (iii) On X_rs(A0), ‖x‖_{X_rs} ∼ ‖x‖_X·‖Δ∘π(x)^{−1}‖, i.e. each side is bounded by a constant times a power of the other. (v) Σ_{b∈B_rs(F0)} ‖b‖_{B_rs}^{−d} < ∞ for d large. (vii) For every d3 > 0 there is d > 0 with ∫_{G(A0)} ‖g·x‖_{X_rs}^{−d} dg ≪ ‖π_rs(x)‖_{B_rs}^{−d3} for x ∈ X_rs(A0). The local analogues hold with constants independent of v and equal to 1 for almost all v. These are [1, Prop. A.1.1(ii),(iii),(v),(vii)] as the proof of Lemma 11.1 uses them; the exact hypotheses must be read from Beuzart-Plessis, Appendix A.1.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 11.1, (11.8)–(11.14), pp. 935–937, citing [1, §A.1, Prop. A.1.1]; also used for Lemma 11.2, p. 939
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): These norm estimates carry the whole convergence argument of Lemmas 11.1 and 11.2, and hence the definition of J. The extraction lists Beuzart-Plessis only as a prerequisite paper, and gate G4 asks for them, but no item states them. Suggested owner: partly: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.0 plans height functions on groups (polynomial comparability) only. The variety and torsor estimates are new; suggested owner is the Jacquet–Rallis Part II (route 9), or EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.1, which plans convergence of regular semisimple orbital integrals Route: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison.

items.name: Higher-rank regular nilpotent orbital integrals
items.statement: Let α ∈ A_n(F0) be irreducible over F, with F′ = F[T]/(α) CM over F0′. Let γ ∈ S_n(α)(F0) have stabilizer T′ ≅ Res_{F0′/F0}G_m, let η′ = η_{F′/F0′}, and fix nonzero u1 ∈ V0(F0) and u2 ∈ V0*(F0). For a place v and Φ′_v ∈ S((S_n×V′)(F0,v)), put Orb((γ,0+),Φ′_v,s) = ∫_{G′(F0,v)} Φ′_v(g^{−1}·(γ,(u1,0)))|det g|_v^s η(g) dg / L(s,η′_v) and Orb((γ,0−),Φ′_v,−s) = ∫_{G′(F0,v)} Φ′_v(g^{−1}·(γ,(0,u2)))|det g|_v^s η(g) dg / L(−s,η′_v). Here L(s,η′_v) = ∏_{v′|v} L(s,η′_{v′}), the Haar measures satisfy vol(G′(O_{F0,v})) = 1 for almost all v, and both integrals are continued analytically (Lemma 12.13). For a pure tensor Φ′, set Orb((γ,0+),Φ′,s) = L(s,η′)∏_v Orb((γ,0+),Φ′_v,s) and Orb((γ,0−),Φ′,s) = L(−s,η′)∏_v Orb((γ,0−),Φ′_v,−s). Let Orb((γ,0±),Φ′,s) be their sum (12.31), and J(h,Φ′,s)_0 = Orb((γ,0±),ω(h)Φ′,s). Here L(s,η′) = L(s, Ind_{F0′}^{F0} η′), and the global products do not depend on the rational representatives u1, u2, by the product formula. The action g^{−1}· is the one for which the 0+ integral converges for Re(s) > 0, namely that of §12.5 (see the issue on action conventions).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): The definition of the higher-rank regular nilpotent orbital integrals, with their L(s,η′_v) normalization and Haar measure, has no item. Items 108–110 use it. Suggested owner: none; owner: the Jacquet–Rallis Part II (route 9), with Tate integrals from AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1 Route: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison.

items.name: Linear orbit expansion and Fourier coefficients
items.statement: Let α, γ and Φ′ = ⊗Φ′_v be as in §12.6, with Φ′_v the partial Gaussian test functions for v | ∞. For h ∈ H(A0) and s ∈ C, J(h,Φ′,s) = Orb((γ,0±),ω(h)Φ′,s) + Σ_{(γ,u′)∈[(S_n(α)×V′)(F0)]_rs} Orb((γ,u′),ω(h)Φ′,s) (12.32). For ξ ∈ F0^×, the ξ-th Fourier coefficient (1.12) of h ↦ J(h,Φ′,s) is Σ_{(γ,u′)∈[(S_n(α)×V′_ξ)(F0)]} Orb((γ,u′),ω(h)Φ′,s) (12.33), where V′_ξ = {q(u′) = ξ}. The nilpotent term contributes only to the constant term.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): This is the orbit expansion of J(h,Φ′,s) and the orbit-sum formula for its ξ-th Fourier coefficient, the linear analogue of (11.15)–(11.16) (item 94). §13 uses it in the proof of Proposition 13.3 and on p. 955, and §14 uses it too. Item 110's statement omits it. Suggested owner: none; owner: the Jacquet–Rallis Part II (route 9) Route: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison.

items.name: Product formula for the global transfer factor
items.statement: Let F/F0 be a CM extension of a totally real field, η = η_{F/F0}, and η̃ a Hecke character of F^×\A_F^× with η̃|_{A_{F0}^×} = η (not necessarily of order 2). For (γ,u′) ∈ (S_n × V′_n)(F0)_rs with u′ = (u1,u2), set x(γ,u′) := det(γ)^{−⌊n/2⌋}·det(u1, γu1, …, γ^{n−1}u1) ∈ F^× and ω_v(γ,u′) := η̃_v(x(γ,u′)). Then ω_v(γ,u′) = 1 for almost all v and ∏_v ω_v(γ,u′) = η̃(x) = 1. Likewise ∏_v ω_v(γ) = 1 for γ ∈ S_n(F0)_rs with (2.16). Moreover ω_v(h·(γ,u′)) = η(det h)^{−1}ω_v(γ,u′) for h ∈ GL_n(F0,v), so the transferred local orbital integrals are well defined on orbits. At an inert v where η̃ is unramified, η̃_v is the natural extension x ↦ (−1)^{v(x)} of §2.3, which is the normalization used in the FL/AFL.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): Theorem 13.4 multiplies local identities over all places, which needs the product formula for the global transfer factor. No item states it: item 7 is local only. Suggested owner: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison (Part II, route 9) Route: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison.

items.name: Elementary transfer at split places
items.statement: Let v be a place of F0 split in F, so that F_v = F0,v × F0,v, U(V_v) ≅ GL_n(F0,v), S_n(F0,v) = {(a,a^{−1})} ≅ GL_n(F0,v), and V_v ≅ F0,v^n × (F0,v^n)^* ≅ V′_n equivariantly. Under these identifications the regular semisimple orbits of S_n × V′_n and U(V_v) × V_v correspond, and every Φ_v ∈ S((U(V_v)×V_v)(F0,v)) has an explicit transfer Φ′_v ∈ S((S_n×V′_n)(F0,v)): Orb((γ,u′),Φ′_v) = Orb((δ,u),Φ_v) for all matching regular semisimple pairs, with the transfer factor of the split place. In particular a pointwise nonnegative Φ_v with prescribed support has a transfer.
items.locator: §13.1, Remark 13.2, p. 953 (used in Proposition 13.8, p. 958, and Lemma 14.2, p. 961)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): Proposition 13.8 (p. 958) needs, for an arbitrary nonnegative Φ̃_{v1} at a split place v1, a matching Φ̃′_{v1} 'in the elementary way', and Lemma 14.2 uses the same matching. Item 8's API mentions split-place elementary transfer, but no item states it. Suggested owner: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison (Part II, route 9) Route: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison.

items.name: Existence of partial transfers relative to α
items.statement: Let v be a non-archimedean place and α ∈ A_n(F0) irreducible. For every Φ_v ∈ S((U(V_v)×V_v)(F0,v)) there is Φ′_v ∈ S((S_n×V′_n)(F0,v)) that partially (relative to α) transfers to Φ_v in the sense of Definition 13.1. Given matching (g,u) and (γ,u′) in the α-fibre, Φ_v and Φ′_v can be chosen with Orb((g,u),Φ_v) = Orb((γ,u′),Φ′_v) ≠ 0. The proof reduces to rank one over F′/F′0 via §12.6. Full transfer is [47], cited as an input.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): The proofs of Theorems 13.9 (p. 960) and 15.1 (p. 969) choose, at v ∈ S, partial transfers with nonvanishing orbital integrals at a given orbit. Their existence (from [47], or from the case n = 1 for fixed α) is not an item. Suggested owner: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison (Part II, route 9) Route: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison.

items.name: Weil invariance of the standard functions at level c_v
items.statement: Let v be a non-archimedean place, F_v/F0,v unramified, Λ ⊂ V_v a self-dual Hermitian lattice, and ψ_v of level c_v. Let K_v = m(ϖ^{c_v})^{-1}SL2(O_{F0,v})m(ϖ^{c_v}) with m(ϖ^c) = diag(ϖ^c,1). Then ω(k)1_{(U(V_v)×V_v)(O)} = 1_{(U(V_v)×V_v)(O)} and ω(k)1_{(S_n×V′_n)(O)} = 1_{(S_n×V′_n)(O)} for all k ∈ K_v (Weil action on the vector variable). In particular both are SL2(O_{F0,v})-invariant when c_v = 0.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): Applying Lemma 13.6 requires the standard functions at v ∉ S to be Weil-invariant under K_v = m(ϖ^{c_v})^{-1}SL2(O)m(ϖ^{c_v}). The paper says only 'it is known'. I checked it: N(ϖ^{-c}O) acts through ψ(bq(x)) with q integral on the lattice, and N^-(ϖ^cO) is conjugated by w to N(ϖ^cO) acting on the ψ-dual lattice ϖ^{-c}Λ. Suggested owner: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison (Part II, route 9); MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.2 supplies the operator formulas Route: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison.

items.name: Strong approximation for SL2 over a number field
items.statement: For a number field F0, SL2(F0)·SL2(F0 ⊗ R) is dense in SL2(A0); equivalently SL2(F0) is dense in SL2(A_{0,f}).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): The base case of Lemma 13.6 uses that H(F0)H(F0,∞) is dense in H(A0). Owner: AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.4

items.name: Generation of SL2 by unipotent subgroups
items.statement: (i) For any field k, SL2(k) is generated by N(k) together with any single element of SL2(k) \ B(k). (ii) For a non-archimedean local field with ring of integers O and uniformizer ϖ, SL2 of the field is generated by N(ϖ^{−1}O) and N^-(O). Equivalently, for every integer c it is generated by N(ϖ^{−c−1}O) and N^-(ϖ^cO).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): Both steps of Lemma 13.6 use generation statements for SL2 that no item covers. Suggested owner: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups (route 3, with item 113) Route: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups.

items.name: Local constancy of relative orbital integrals
items.statement: Let F0 be non-archimedean. For Φ′ ∈ S((S_n × V′_n)(F0)), the functions (γ,u′) ↦ Orb((γ,u′),Φ′) and (γ,u′) ↦ ∂Orb((γ,u′),Φ′) (special value and derivative at s = 0, transfer factor included) are locally constant on (S_n × V′_n)(F0)_rs. For Φ ∈ S((U(V)×V)(F0)), (g,u) ↦ Orb((g,u),Φ) is locally constant on (U(V)×V)(F0)_rs. The same holds for the group versions on S_n and U(V^♯).
items.locator: §13.5, proof of Theorem 13.9, pp. 960–961; §15, proof of Theorem 15.1, p. 969
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): Both globalizations and both density extensions need local constancy of the analytic orbital integrals and their derivatives on the regular semisimple locus. Item 39 covers only Int (Theorem 5.5). Suggested owner: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison (Part II, route 9) Route: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison.

items.name: Hermitian spaces with prescribed local data
items.statement: Let F/F0 be a CM extension of number fields. (i) Given finitely many places and a local Hermitian class at each (with a signature prescribed at the real places), there is a global one-dimensional Hermitian space realising them; for dimension one, choose a ∈ F0^× by weak approximation. (ii) (Landherr) An n-dimensional global F/F0-Hermitian space exists with prescribed local spaces V_v for all v (almost all split, the signatures at ∞ prescribed) if and only if ∏_v η_v(det V_v) = 1, and it is unique up to isometry. In particular the v0-nearby space of a global Hermitian space V(v0) exists and differs from V(v0) exactly at v0 and at one archimedean place.
items.locator: §13.5, proof of Theorem 13.9, p. 959; §15, proof of Theorem 15.1, p. 968
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): Existence of the one-dimensional W with local conditions (Theorem 13.9) and of the nearby global space V (split at v0, signature (n−1,1) at ∞, equal to V(v0) elsewhere; Theorem 15.1) requires the Hasse principle for Hermitian spaces (Landherr) and weak approximation. Owner: GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.2

items.name: Incoherence of the §14 test data
items.statement: Let V be the n-dimensional F/F0-Hermitian space of the Shimura datum (signature (n−1,1) at one archimedean place, positive definite at the others). Let Φ′ = ⊗Φ′_v have partial Gaussian components at every v | ∞, and let Φ′_v partially (relative to α) transfer to Φ_v ∈ S((U(V_v)×V_v)(F0,v)) at every finite v. Then no global F/F0-Hermitian space Ṽ has Φ′ transferring to S((U(Ṽ)×Ṽ)(A0)): the local spaces (V_v for v finite, positive definite for v | ∞) have product of local invariants −1. Consequently, for every regular semisimple (γ,u′) ∈ (S_n(α)×V′)(F0) and every place v split in F, ∏_{w≠v} Orb((γ,u′),Φ′_w) = 0. For non-split v, the product over w ≠ v can be nonzero only if (γ,u′) matches an element of the v-nearby space V(v).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): This is the mechanism behind Lemma 14.2 (item 118) and behind the orbit bijection in Lemma 14.4 and Theorem 14.6. It is not an item. Suggested owner: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison (Part II, route 9) Route: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison.

items.name: Local derivative Fourier coefficients
items.statement: For a place v of F0, ξ ∈ F0 and h ∈ H(A0), set ∂J_v(ξ,h,Φ′) := Σ_{(γ,u′)∈[(S_n(α)×V′_ξ)(F0)], u′≠0} ∂Orb((γ,u′),ω(h_v)Φ′_v)·Orb((γ,u′),ω(h^v)Φ′^v), so that ∂J_v(h,Φ′) = Σ_{ξ∈F0} ∂J_v(ξ,h,Φ′) ((14.1)–(14.2)). For finite non-split v, ∂J_v(ξ,h,Φ′) = 0 unless ξ ≥ 0, and ∂J♭_v(τ,Φ′) = Σ_{ξ≥0} ∂J_v(ξ,Φ′)q^ξ with ∂J_v(ξ,Φ′) := Σ ∂Orb((γ,u′),Φ′_v)·Orb((γ,u′),Φ′^{v,∞}) ((14.4)–(14.5)). This is the coefficient at h_f = 1 divided by the archimedean weight-n Whittaker function (Mihatsch–Zhang (8.20)–(8.22)). For v | ∞, the same normalized coefficient is the one in Lemma 14.4.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): Theorem 14.6(b) and Lemma 14.4 are statements about ∂J_v(ξ,Φ′), which no item defines. Item 110 covers only (12.31)–(12.38). The Whittaker normalization matters for the Gaussian correction (Mihatsch–Zhang (8.20)). Suggested owner: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison (Part II, route 9) Route: JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison.

items.name: Supported cup product
items.statement: For a noetherian formal scheme X and closed formal subschemes Y, Z, the tensor product of complexes of locally free sheaves induces a biadditive map ∪: K_0^Y(X) × K_0^Z(X) → K_0^{Y∩Z}(X), [F·] ∪ [G·] = [F· ⊗ G·] (Gillet–Soulé [11, §1.4]). It is compatible with the relations (short exact sequences and quasi-isomorphisms), associative and commutative, and compatible with enlarging supports. For regular X, under K_0^{Y∩Z}(X) ≅ K′_0(Y∩Z) it sends ([O_Y],[O_Z]) to Σ_j (−1)^j [Tor_j^{O_X}(O_Y,O_Z)] = Y ∩^L_X Z (B.5).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21 (coverage of the paper): The cup product is a separate construction, used in (B.3) and in the derived intersections (B.4)–(B.5) behind every Int in the paper. It appears only in item 129's API. Suggested owner: FormalSupportedIntersections (Part II, route 10) Route: FormalSupportedIntersections.

routes.reason: Generic Hermitian forms, trace quadratic forms, self-dual lattices and local/global classification belong to GN.2. The relative orbit and RZ applications import them.

AL.0 owns local/adelic Schwartz, Fourier and parameter-integration tools, including the Bessel/Mellin calculation needed here; AL.1 owns the normalized Tate integrals and functional equations. Existing real Gaussian/Poisson tools are reused, not replanned as absent.

The coefficient-valued holomorphic SL2 spaces and Fourier uniqueness/vanishing criterion are generic automorphic infrastructure. Lemma13.6 uses strong approximation and local root-group generation, not an AFL hypothesis.

The Weil operator, index, global product formula and theta kernel are explicitly inside these existing layers. Relative transfer compatibility and the AFL comparison consume them rather than recreating the representation.

Reuse the generic Green-divisor and arithmetic-degree/pairing interface also requested by PAPER-ANDREATTA-GOREN-HOWARD-ETAL-18. routes.brief:
Start beyond Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison), importing only generic conjugacy/measure infrastructure from ET.0–ET.1, not an assumed relative FL from ET.3. Import Hermitian local/global forms from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2, Fourier/Tate theory from AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.0–AL.1, Weil operators and theta convergence from MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.2/MP.4/MP.5, and automorphic spaces/Fourier uniqueness from AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.0/AF.2/AF.3. Construct the group, Lie and semi-Lie relative quotients and matching; raw versus transferred orbital integrals with ηdet twist; strongly regular loci; relative Cayley charts and integral rank reduction. Prove local smooth/partial transfer and the Fourier compatibility of AppendixA with the Hermitian-discriminant sign. Construct the fixed-α partially linearized RTF, its regular-orbit absolute/local uniform convergence, nilpotent Tate regularization, rank-one and CM-field reduction, and entire SL2-automorphic J_s. Use Mihatsch–Zhang DOI10.4171/JEMS/1375 §7.2's corrected Gaussians; repair the Weyl/sign descent in §12.4 before treating Lemma12.6 as proved. Do not assert full archimedean Gaussian-transfer existence, which this paper only expects. Endpoints: Theorem12.14 entire modularity; Proposition13.3 holomorphic coherent weight-n series; Theorem13.4 conditional comparison; Theorem13.9 group/semi-Lie FL for unramified quadratic p-adic fields with odd residue characteristic and q≥n. The FL extends to all relative regular orbits by density; the arithmetic consumer's AFL does not thereby extend. Include the exact residue-cardinality bound and all group/semi-Lie rank shifts. Tests: n=1 corrected Bessel integral and derivative; transfer scaling by η(a)^n; n=2 Weyl-fibre counterexample and repaired descent; norm-unit lower-rank reduction; product of rational transfer factors1. This analytic owner has no dependence on RZ spaces or the AFL, preventing circular proof of its FL input.

Corrections from the review (REV-PAPER-ZHANG-21), to respect when stating the layers:
- Proposition 4.12(i) and Proposition 2.7(i) at q = n: the printed proof picks ξ ∈ F¹ with det(1 − ξg′) a unit, but it also needs 1 − ξd to be a unit, which can fail for every admissible ξ when q = n (FL counterexample with q = n = 3). So the reduction '(b) for V_{n−1} ⇒ (a) for V_n' is proved only for q ≥ n + 1. Plan the q = n case separately: for the FL it is covered by Beuzart-Plessis's independent proof; for the AFL at p = n (Theorem 15.1(a)) the printed argument leaves a gap.
- Theorem 5.5 (local constancy) is proved as printed only for q ≥ n; cite Mihatsch (Algebra Number Theory 16 (2022)) in general.
- Lemma 4.3(iii) and Lemma 4.9(iii) need det(1 − g) ≠ 0, and Lemma 4.10's 'srs' holds only for all but finitely many ξ.
- The Gaussian test functions of §12 must use Mihatsch–Zhang's corrected normalisation (E12): for ψ(x) = e^{2πix}, (12.4), Lemmas 12.5 and 12.11 and 'φ̂ = φ' are false as printed; (8.11) needs 4π, not 2π.
- §11.4 and §12.5 use opposite sign conventions for the action on V′, so the regular and nilpotent derivatives in (12.38) must be normalised consistently; Lemma 12.6 omits the archimedean transfer-factor phase for n ≥ 2.
- Propositions 2.7(ii) and 4.12(ii) are applied in §13 at places where their printed q-bound fails; their proofs do not use the bound, so state them without it.

review.reason: Checked against Mihatsch–Zhang, fetched with the stated User-Agent (SHA-256 67c39ae1…, as in result.json). Their (7.6), p. 48, has φ′(x,y) = 2^{−1}(x+y)e^{−π(x²+y²)} with ψ0(b) = exp(2πib). Footnote 5 reads: 'Here the Gaussian functions differ slightly from those in [35, Section 12]; the latter should be corrected accordingly' ([35] is this paper). Footnote 3, p. 18, says the same of the constants. Independent check: take ψ(t) = e^{2πit}, q(x,y) = xy, the pairing xy′ + x′y and the self-dual measure dx dy. Then e^{−c(x²+y²)} is Fourier-fixed only for c = π; the printed c = π/2 goes to 2e^{−2π(x²+y²)}. So the printed φ′ is not an eigenvector of w = κ_{π/2}. This falsifies the weight-1 claim before Lemma 12.5, and the SL2 formulas of Lemmas 12.5 and 12.11, for the stated ψ. The unitary side fails the same way. By (1.4), ⟨u,u⟩ = q(u) is the hermitian norm. For V = C, with pairing 2Re(z w̄) and self-dual measure 2 dx dy, the transform of e^{−πzz̄} is 2e^{−4πzz̄}; so 'φ̂ = φ' and (12.4) fail, and e^{−2πq} is the fixed Gaussian. The printed §12 is internally consistent with ψ(t) = e^{πit}, not with the stated ψ(t) = e^{2πit} and the Whittaker function (1.5): both orbital values are e^{−πξ}, and Lemma 14.3 inherits this. Suppose instead ⟨u,u⟩ in (12.1) is read as the bilinear form 2q(u), as in §11.1. Then the unitary side is right, but Lemma 12.6's matching fails, e^{−πξ} against e^{−2πξ}. On either reading a printed claim is false. The main theorems survive after the rescaling, and Mihatsch–Zhang redo the comparison in §§7–8. The author preprint has the same functions. Minor: Mihatsch–Zhang's text on p. 48 cites '[33, Section 12]' and '[33, Lemma 12.5]'; their [33] is Zhang's 2012 Invent. Math. paper, and the footnote's [35] is meant. Known: Mihatsch–Zhang §7.2 (7.6), Proposition 7.4 and footnote 5, p. 48; footnote 3, p. 18; §7.3, p. 49.

In §12.6, Ω_v is a small neighbourhood of one γ, so this suffices. sourceIssues.locator: Appendix B.2, Lemma B.1 and its proof, p. 974 (with the inverse-limit K-groups of B.1, p. 973)
sourceIssues.printed: Lemma B.1. Let X be a locally noetherian formal schemes of the above type. … Proof. We immediately reduce the question to the case when X is noetherian, which we assume now.
sourceIssues.correction: State Lemma B.1 (and Lemma B.2(ii)) for noetherian X, or define the quotients for locally noetherian X as inverse limits of the noetherian cokernels. The paper uses nothing beyond this: Lemma B.2 is used only in its local form (i), in the proof of Lemma 4.4, p. 889.
sourceIssues.reason: For locally noetherian X, B.1 defines K′_0(X) = lim_i K′_0(X_i), and footnote 11 says the quotients in Lemma B.1 are cokernels. Cokernels do not commute with inverse limits: comparing coker(lim) with lim(coker) involves a lim^1 term. Moreover, for an element of lim_i K′_0(X_i), 'E ⊗ O_{X1}' is defined at each stage only modulo the image of K′_0(X1∩X2∩X_i). So the reduction to the noetherian case is not immediate, and a proof would need a Mittag-Leffler argument that the paper does not give. The noetherian case itself is proved correctly.
